SMK37 Pro / Elite · 37 keys · 16 pads · 8 encoders · 4 faders. FADER BANK: tracks 1–4 / 5–8, with pickup. KNOB BANK + CHORD: LFO; KNOB BANK + PATCH: source; KNOB BANK + SEQ: MIDI channels; KNOB BANK + Pads: track / mute.

Drag or scroll knobs. Click LCD values to edit.Controls guide
Start with these three steps
  1. Play: hold KNOB BANK and tap NOTE REPEAT to enter or leave the Pad instrument (NOTE REPEAT alone, held, repeats a held key or pad). KEY defaults to track 1 / channel 1 and PAD to track 8 / channel 10. K5 and OCTAVE adjust only the instrument being edited.
  2. Shape a sound: tap PARA and turn K1–K4. For a different engine, use KNOB BANK + PATCH, choose with Pads 1–6 or K1, then > to apply.
  3. Play a song: write a song in the web workbench or import a MIDI file and write it to the device, then press SEQ and PARA together, choose SONG MODE and press SEQ PLAY on the SONG page.

Pad aftertouch follows the Pad channel; DX7 responds with vibrato. In the browser, hold a Pad and drag upward to preview aftertouch, or press with a pressure-sensitive pen.

When a fader shows UP TO / DOWN TO, move it through the target to take control without an abrupt volume jump. F1–F4 identify faders; T1–T8 identify their tracks.

            Waiting for a device with project-library support.

            Bluetooth settings

            The device's Bluetooth page is gone; changes here are written to the device and saved at once. The clock source is on the device's SYNC / MIDI page (press SEQ).

            Full backup and restore (Classic Tabby)

            One file holds everything on the device: the 16 project slots (slot 16 carries the device settings), the unsaved workspace and the current slot, the device and session settings (MIDI configuration, track roles, input channels, panel preferences: on the diagnostic build and later), the Bluetooth switches, every song record and block, and the firmware's build ID and layout. Your "My rig" profile from this browser goes in too. Not in the file: Bluetooth pairings, the built-in rig profiles (they come with the workbench). Stop song playback first. A backup loads each project slot in turn and puts your workspace back at the end. Format: docs/BACKUP-FORMAT.md (version 1).

              Diagnostics (timing counters and control-loop profile)

              Timing counters and the control-loop profile (every build from tabby-v04.0; docs/BUILD.md 24.6 and 26.4). Reset, play for the time the measurement needs, then Read. The flash part line gives the flash chip’s JEDEC ID and size as the device read them at start-up (from tabby-v04.9.3); it is a report and changes nothing. Each section of the profile is the time per control pass spent in that part of the app, mean and longest; "SDK between the hooks" is the rest of the pass. Times in milliseconds; the counter runs at 24 MHz. Reading is allowed while the device plays.

              

              Device projects

              

              





Loading or restoring replaces the unsaved workspace. Restoring a file does not write a device slot automatically; save it when ready.

              

              Track sounds

              

              

Includes the engine, sound parameters and level, without steps. Switching between drum and melodic engines clears incompatible steps on this track. PATCH + > undoes the import on the panel.

              

              Standard DX7 patches

              

              


Supports DX7 single-voice and 32-voice bank SysEx; extension parameters are not handled. Set the target track to DX7 first. After importing, save the project for PROJECT tracks; for LIVE tracks, export a timbre file or save the voice to the independent DX7 library.

              

              Rig setup (Classic Tabby)

              Tells the workbench which device sits on each MIDI channel (definitions in web/devices/: program numbering, banks, named CCs, the gap a device needs). The row event editor then picks presets by name. The profile is saved in this browser, exportable as JSON; a song can carry its own copy. The panel is in English.
              

              

              

              Song mode (Classic Tabby)

              A song is a sequence of rows; each row assigns one block (64 steps, up to 4 notes per step) to each of the 8 tracks. Songs live in the device's song storage and play from the panel's ACTIONS > SONG MODE. File format: docs/tasks/TASK-03-step1-assessment.md section 9.
              

              Clip launching: on the device BT opens the CLIPS page (SCALE from the SONG page too). Pads 1-16 are the selected track's clips of the current bank (OCTAVE banks); a pad launches its clip at the next master cycle, pressing the playing clip's pad stops it at the next cycle; KNOB BANK + pads 1-8 select the track; CHORD sends the selected track back to the song, KNOB BANK + CHORD every track; a scene jump (SONG page) overrides every track queue. A device's "Lead ms" makes its program change leave before the bar.
              

              

              



              


              Song storage holds OLD DATA: flash that is not in the song format (left by V01, V16, the storage move or an interrupted write). Songs cannot be written or played until it is erased. Projects, tunings and device settings are not touched. If you have not made a Full backup yet, make one first.
              

              

              



              

              Scenes and clips: each row is a scene; every block a track uses is a clip of that track (64 per track). Launches, stops and scene recalls on the device land on the next multiple of the master cycle (16 steps = one bar of 4/4). A song stored as rows always uses a cycle of 16 steps.
              

              

              

              


              RowT1T2T3T4T5T6T7T8RepeatStepsLoop here
              


              


              

              


              Per step: pitch:velocity:length[r], several notes separated by spaces; r = retrigger, @n = probability n/8, ! = alt tuning (example: 60:100:2 64:100:2r @4). Lengths are in 16th steps.
              

              

              Step text: pitch:velocity:length/offset; length in steps (decimals allowed, 1/480 step resolution), offset in signed units (1 unit = 1/480 step), r = retrigger, @n = probability n/8, ! = alt tuning. Steps with an offset or a fractional length carry an orange mark on the left; click a step to edit its notes in the inspector below.
              

              


              

              
Write song stores the song record first, then every block in the editor in batches (up to 8 sectors per batch, one commit each; old copies are reclaimed by ACTIONS > COMPACT SONG STORAGE on the device), then verifies the record by read-back. Device audio pauses briefly while it writes. Restoring factory V16 overwrites the last 40 KB of song storage (block sectors 70 to 79 of the 80, flash 0xF4000 to 0xFDFFF): export your songs first.

              

              Import MIDI file (Classic Tabby)

              Converts a standard MIDI file (.mid, type 0/1, Renoise exports included) into a song: preview the parts, assign tracks and output channels, pick a bar range, then write to the device or the browser simulator (the target follows the Song mode target above; an occupied song slot is deleted first). The panel is in English.

              00 · What changed in tabby-v04
              

              This chapter lists what tabby-v04.0, tabby-v04.1, tabby-v04.2, tabby-v04.3.1, tabby-v04.4, tabby-v04.5, tabby-v04.6, tabby-v04.7 (with tabby-v04.7.1), tabby-v04.8 and tabby-v04.9 (with tabby-v04.9.1, tabby-v04.9.2 and tabby-v04.9.3) changed compared with tabby-v03.x. The chapters after it have the details. The page you are on is tabby-v1.3. The testing and user guide has set-up, the device steps in order and a numbered test checklist.
              

                

              • The storage move. User storage went from 536576 to 471040 bytes: 16 project slots plus 97 song-region sectors (80 of them block sectors). Installing tabby-v04.0 over v03.x once clears the project slots, the device settings and the songs, so restore them from a Full backup; Bluetooth pairings are lost too. Later updates, tabby-v04.1 included, do not move storage again. See chapter 11.
                • 

              • The old pattern editing and recording are gone. (From tabby-v04.8 the clips of a song are edited on the new STEP page, and from tabby-v04.9 SEQ REC records into a clip; both in chapter 05.) The STEP DETAILS, LOCKS and RHYTHM/SEQ REC pages, SEQ REC recording, the count-in, the metronome, pad-step mode and the copy, paste, clear, repeat and undo menu entries are gone. Patterns already in a project still load, save and play. The metronome and count-in are planned for a later version.
                • 

              • The SYNC / MIDI page. Press SEQ on any page: K1 CLOCK, K2 CLK IN, K3 SWING, K4 SEQ OUT, K7 KEY OUT. KNOB BANK + SEQ opens MIDI TRACK and SEQ + PARA together open ACTIONS. Tempo is set only with K4 on the overview; PATCH + SEQ taps it.
                • 

              • STOP TO SAVE. While a song or a pattern plays, the device writes nothing to flash: saving shows STOP TO SAVE, and erase and compaction show STOP TO ERASE / COMPACT. The workbench refuses writes too and says the device is playing and nothing was written. Stop playback, then try again.
                • 

              • OLD DATA and erasing. If song storage still holds old data after an install, the device shows OLD DATA IN SONG STORAGE: press SEQ and PARA together to open ACTIONS, choose ERASE OLD DATA and confirm twice with >. The workbench button for erasing old data does the same. Projects, tunings and settings are not touched.
                • 

              • The timing counters. Every build carries the control-loop and flash timing counters, which the workbench and the diagnostic tools can read. tabby-v04.1 cuts the screen drawing and transfer work in each 10 ms control pass into slices, always sends song notes and MIDI first, and adds busy-time and lost-tick counters. CPU GUARD - VOICES ADAPTED on the screen is the sound engine’s CPU budget guard; it only lowers the internal voice count and does not change what is sent on MIDI.
                • 

              • The flash part (tabby-v04.9.3). Diagnostics has one more line: the flash chip’s JEDEC ID and size, as the device read them when it started. It is for reports only. The firmware works the same with any chip of 1 MiB; nothing checks this line.
                • 

              • Fast MIDI (tabby-v04.2). Notes of a song used to wait for the next 10 ms control pass before they left the MIDI out. tabby-v04.2 asks for that pass at once from the audio engine, so a single line leaves about 3.7 ms after it is due instead of about 12 ms (measured on a device, DIN out). Eight lines at the same step leave within about 6.5 ms. It is on at power-up. ACTIONS has an entry, A2 FAST MIDI: ON or OFF, that switches it for this session only. The Diagnostics counters show it: how many requests it made, what each call cost and how often a call was repeated.
                • 

              • Remote control over USB (tabby-v04.2). The workbench transfer link has a command to read the screen page and the song state, select a song, start or stop it, jump to a row, switch fast MIDI and press, hold or release a named panel control, so tests can run without anyone at the panel. It writes nothing to flash, and it refuses > (SAVE). A control it holds is released by itself after 5 seconds without a command.
                • 

              • External clock in song mode (tabby-v04.3.1). With CLOCK set to MIDI (SEQ, K1) and a song chosen on the SONG page, SEQ PLAY arms the song: the page shows ARMED: START? The master then runs it. Each clock pulse moves the song; Start begins at the first pulse; Continue resumes where it stopped; Stop stops at once and releases all notes, and always wins; Song Position Pointer moves the song, running or stopped. If clock pulses stop for about three pulses the song holds and releases its notes (HOLD: NO CLOCK); if they return within 2 seconds it carries on from where it held; after 2 seconds it shows LOST - CONTINUE and only Continue or Start restarts it, never the pulses alone. The clock comes in over USB or Bluetooth; the TRS jack is output only. At the end of the song it arms again for the next Start.
                • 

              • Timed MIDI (tabby-v04.4). Every note, row event and clock byte of a song now carries the time it is due, and a 0.5 ms timer sends it then, one audio block (2.9 ms) after the engine found it. A single line keeps its timing within about 1.9 ms and eight lines at the same step within about 3 ms (measured on a device, DIN and USB out), whatever page the screen shows; before, it was about 5 ms and up to 7.5 ms and depended on the page. Notes that are due together leave as one burst. With CLOCK on MIDI the song is kept one block ahead of the master's pulses, so its notes still leave at their pulses. A2 FAST MIDI on ACTIONS switches all of it off and on for the session. Firmware Update and the workbench work with CLOCK on INT or on MIDI.
                • 

              • Larger clips (tabby-v04.5). The part a track plays in a row is a clip. A clip can now hold any number of notes on a step (it was four), controller, pitch bend and aftertouch events, a program and bank of its own (sent once when the track enters the clip, with its first note), and up to 128 steps; a row can be 16 to 128 steps. Such a clip is stored in a new form (a v3 clip, up to 512 events) and the device plays it straight from its event list. The MIDI importer writes a v3 clip only where a part needs one, and keeps controller events when its box is ticked; everything else is stored as before, and old songs play unchanged. The step editor shows clips of up to 64 steps and four notes per step; it keeps a larger clip as it is. Full backup, restore and .tabby files carry v3 clips. A song with v3 clips or rows of more than 64 steps needs tabby-v04.5 or later on the device.
                • 

              • Scenes and clips (tabby-v04.6). A song can be stored as scenes: every track has up to 64 clips (the device will show them in banks of 16), and a scene names one clip per track, with a length of 16 to 128 steps and a repeat count. A song has up to 128 scenes; played in order they are the song. The song also has a master cycle (16 steps unless you change it; one bar of the file's metre when imported): a track launch, a track stop, back to the song and a scene recall land on its next multiple. In Song mode choose "Stored as: scenes and clips" and set the master cycle; the MIDI importer writes scenes when its box is ticked, with clips of up to 8 bars. Songs stored as rows play as before, and the device never changes a stored song by itself: a song becomes scenes only when you write it again from this page. A song stored as scenes needs tabby-v04.6 or later on the device.
                • 

              • Clip launching (tabby-v04.7). BT opens the CLIPS page from anywhere: the pads show the selected track's clips, 16 of up to 64 at a time (off empty, dim white stopped, green playing, blinking green queued, blinking red a stop queued, bright the selected clip, orange when the track is muted). A pad launches its clip or stops the playing one at the next master cycle; a blinking pad pressed again takes that back; a pad held half a second selects only. On the SONG page the pads light up and recall scenes. KNOB BANK + pad 9 to 16 now also holds a muted track's song notes back on MIDI out. A clip that no scene uses can be launched too. Chapter 05 has the page; docs/CONTROL-MAP.md in the source has every control. tabby-v04.7.1: a pad pressed while the song is stopped reserves its clip and SEQ PLAY starts it (as on the MC-707); the two mutes look different (orange: sound and song notes; blue: internal sound only).
                • 

              • Editing clips on the device (tabby-v04.8). PARA on the CLIPS page opens the STEP page on the selected clip. The 16 pads are the steps of a bar; press one, then play keys to enter or remove notes on it; K1 to K4 choose a note and set its velocity, start and length; FX undoes (four levels). The edit is heard without saving, and is saved when the song is stopped. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • Recording (tabby-v04.9). SEQ REC on the CLIPS or STEP page records what you play into the selected clip while it loops: the keys and pads, and notes, controllers, pitch bend and channel pressure from MIDI in on the track's channel. Notes go to the nearest step (input quantize; KNOB BANK+SEQ REC switches it off). A take is one undo level. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • Clip workflow on the panel (tabby-v04.10). SEQ REC or PARA on an empty pad makes a new clip. FX on CLIPS opens CLIP SETTING: the clip's length, a copy to another pad, and the song's click and count-in. Holding an empty pad on SCENES stores what plays as a new scene. Every clip now loops at its own length. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • Clip chains (tabby-v04.11). CLIP SETTING has NEXT CLIP (STAY, STOP or a clip), AFTER (the clip's end, or a number of steps) and TIMES: a launched clip leads to the next one by itself. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • The scene chain (tabby-v04.12). On SCENES, K1 sets how many times a scene plays, K2 whether the next scene follows by itself, K3 holds the chain. A scene pad pressed while stopped is where SEQ PLAY starts. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • Transpose and delete a clip (tabby-v04.15). CLIP SETTING has TRANSPOSE (a clip's notes up or down by as much as 12 semitones when it plays; the clip itself is not changed) and DELETE CLIP (> twice, while stopped; a clip a scene uses is never deleted). Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • Click level, controller numbers, a clearer backup (tabby-v04.14). CLICK LEVEL sets the internal click to LOW, MID or HIGH. K1 CONTROLLER to K4 CONTROLLER choose, per song, what the four knobs on CLIPS send. CLIP SETTING is two pages: the clip's lines and the song's lines. The Full backup names a song this page cannot read and stops. The MIDI importer keeps a clip's own length and its chain when it rewrites a song. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • Delete and move a scene; a stop ends an armed take (tabby-v04.16). On SCENES, with the song stopped, FX twice deletes the selected scene and PARA held with K1 moves it earlier or later. A take that was armed while the song played is taken off when the song stops. The guide is also one printable PDF. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • Shuffle and play quantize for each clip (tabby-v04.17). CLIP SETTING has SHUFFLE (the song's swing, or the clip's own from 0 to 50 percent) and PLAY QUANTIZE (OFF, 1/16, 1/8, 1/4: the notes start on the grid when the clip plays; the clip itself is not changed). The page now has three pages. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • tabby-v1.3: take after take without stopping. Until now a second clip could not be opened, recorded or made while one was unsaved, and nothing is saved while a song plays: one take a song. Now eight clips can be unsaved at once; they play as edited and are all saved when you stop. The firmware also keeps a record of the latest any timed MIDI event ever left, with what the SMK-37 was doing then (read by the test tools).
                • 

              • tabby-v1.2.1: a message goes when you press anything. Any press on the panel (a button, a pad, a key, a knob) takes a message away at once, and PLAY / STOP / REC stays readable at the left end of the message while it is up. A track whose internal sound is muted, or silenced by a solo, no longer loads the sound engine while a song plays.
                • 

              • tabby-v1.2: messages at the top; the screen proven on the device. A message is now an amber box across the top, over the top line, so it never covers the pads' cells; it stays about a second and a half as before. The firmware can give back the pixels it sent to its screen (a remote command that only reads); the release test compares them with this simulator's on every page, stopped and playing, and the manual's pictures are taken from the device that way.
                • 

              • tabby-v1.1: a screen you can read on stage. Nothing on the screen is smaller than 10 x 14 pixels a character any more (it was 5 x 7). The tempo, PLAY / STOP / REC, the selected track, the song and scene, queued launches and every message are half as large again. Pages show fewer things: the key help left the screen (it is here and in the guide), CLIP SETTING has four pages of eight lines, and the pages with four knobs show one line per knob with its full name and a large value. Messages are an amber box (across the top from tabby-v1.2). Some lines are shorter: PLAY QUANT, CLICK CH, K1 CC to K4 CC, REC ONLY, FWD+REV. Chapters 04 and 05 describe the SONG and CLIPS pages as they are now; the manual has pictures of every page.
                • 

              • tabby-v1.0.2: EVENT LEAD. A song setting on CLIP SETTING (page 4/4, the last line): OFF, 1/32, 1/16, 1/8 or 1/4. A scene's program changes, bank select and controllers go out that long before the scene's downbeat, so that its first notes do not wait behind them on a shared DIN cable. It is OFF unless you set it, and with OFF a song plays exactly as on tabby-v1.0.1. With a lead the synth changes its sound that much early: the last notes of the scene before are heard on the new sound. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • tabby-v1.0.1: scene events in a two-scene loop. A song of two scenes that loops sends each scene's row events (program changes, bank select, controllers) at every entry of the scene. tabby-v1.0 and tabby-v04.23 sent them on the first pass and then only now and then; older versions have the same code. Songs with three or more scenes in a row were not affected.
                • 

              • tabby-v1.0: the release for the stage. No new function. What KNOB BANK with a pad says (TRACK SELECTED, TRACK MUTED - SOUND + MIDI, TRACK UNMUTED) is now written in the first line of the KNOB BANK list, where it can be seen while the button is held; before, it was written on the line the list covers. Pads 1 to 8 are the upper row (confirmed on a unit). The guide has a one-page stage checklist (its section 9).
                • 

              • The step loop (tabby-v04.23). On CLIPS, while the song plays, hold NOTE REPEAT and hold pad 9, 10, 11 or 12: every track that plays repeats its last 1, 2, 4 or 8 steps for as long as the pad is down (STEP LOOP: LAST 4 STEPS). Let go and the song goes on where it would have been. Not during a take. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • Note repeat (tabby-v04.22). NOTE REPEAT does what is printed on it: while you hold it, a key or pad you hold repeats at the track's ARP rate (K1 while it is held: 1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32). The switch between keys and pads moved to KNOB BANK+NOTE REPEAT. Note repeat is the track's arpeggiator switched on while the button is down: one held note repeats, several take turns; GATE, SWING, DIRECTION and RANGE of the ARP page apply.
                • 

              • Clearing notes in a take, shifting a clip, a new song (tabby-v04.21). During a take, FX held with a key clears that key's notes as the clip passes them. On the STEP page KNOB BANK+OCTAVE+ or OCTAVE- shifts the whole clip by a step. ACTIONS has NEW SONG: an empty song in an empty slot. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • Direction for each clip (tabby-v04.20). CLIP SETTING has DIRECTION: FORWARD, REVERSE, or FWD THEN REV (forwards, then backwards, twice as long). The clip itself is not changed. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • Step size for each clip (tabby-v04.19). CLIP SETTING has STEP SIZE: what one step of the clip lasts: 1/16, 1/8 (half speed), 1/32 (double speed) or the triplet sizes 1/16T and 1/8T. The MC-707 calls it SCALE. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • The printed button names (tabby-v04.18). The screen, this Help and the guide call every button by the word printed on it. No function changed; firmware before tabby-v04.18 shows the earlier names on its screen (the item Control names lists them).
                • 

              • Going back to an older build. Songs saved on the device by tabby-v04.10 or later cannot be read by older firmware. Go back only with a Full backup made before tabby-v04.10: install the older build, then restore that backup.
                • 

              • Program, bank and controller knobs (tabby-v04.13). CLIP SETTING has PROGRAM, BANK MSB and BANK LSB for each clip. On CLIPS, K1 to K4 send controllers 74, 71, 1 and 11, and a take records them. Chapter 05 has the details.
                • 

              • Recovery pages. Every published build has a permanent page under builds/, and the builds/ page lists them all. If an install is interrupted, the device’s update loader accepts only the build it was receiving: close this page, power-cycle the device, then open the page of that build. Never force flash; the Enable force flash and reconnect button is gone.
                • 

              • Control names. Knobs are called K1 to K8 by their printed numbers, from the left; the firmware’s SELECT is K5, PAGE is K6, PRESETS is K7 and MASTER is K8. Buttons are called by the words printed on them, on the device screen too (from tabby-v04.18): KNOB BANK, FADER BANK, <, >, OCTAVE- and OCTAVE+ in the left group; ARP, NOTE REPEAT, SCALE, CHORD, GLOBE, BT, PATCH, PARA, FX, SEQ, SEQ PLAY and SEQ REC in the right group. > saves and confirms; < does what PATCH does when pressed alone, but KNOB BANK + PATCH (the sound source page) works with PATCH only. Earlier versions used the firmware’s names: SHIFT for KNOB BANK, HOME for PATCH and <, “the 4th button in the left group” for >, OCT - and OCT + for OCTAVE- and OCTAVE+, PAD / STEP for NOTE REPEAT, SCL for SCALE, ENV for CHORD, MIX for GLOBE, HOME / SRC for PATCH, EDIT for PARA, PLAY for SEQ PLAY and REC for SEQ REC.
                • 

              

              01 · What Classic Tabby is
              

              Classic Tabby is a performance MIDI sequencer firmware for the M-VAVE SMK-37 Pro. It is a fork of SMK37 Open V01. It works like a Roland MC-707 that plays outside gear over MIDI: a song has eight tracks, each track has clips, a scene is one clip per track, and everything you launch lands on the next master cycle. Songs are imported from MIDI files or built on the panel, and both can be edited and recorded into on the device.
              

              What it does
              

                

              • Holds 16 songs. A song has 8 tracks, up to 64 clips per track and up to 128 scenes. A clip is 1 to 128 steps long and holds up to 512 events: notes, controller moves, pitch bend, pressure.
                • 

              • Launches and stops clips from the pads of the CLIPS page, and recalls scenes from the pads of the SCENES page, always on the next master cycle (one bar unless the song says otherwise).
                • 

              • Plays the scenes in order by itself (the scene chain: each scene a number of times, then the next), and lets a launched clip lead to another one (clip chains).
                • 

              • Edits a clip on the STEP page (pads are steps, keys enter notes, four undo levels) and records into a clip from the keys or from outside gear, with input quantize, a click and a count-in.
                • 

              • Makes new clips, copies them, changes their length, and stores what plays as a new scene, all on the panel.
                • 

              • Keeps note starts and lengths to 1/480 of a 16th step and sends each note within about 2 ms of its time.
                • 

              • Sends a program change and bank select when a track enters a clip, and program changes, bank selects and control changes when a scene starts, with the gaps your gear needs and a lead before the bar.
                • 

              • Sends four controllers from K1 to K4 on the CLIPS page (the numbers are the song's), and records them in a take.
                • 

              • Is the clock master (MIDI Clock, Start, Stop, Song Position Pointer), or follows a clock from USB or Bluetooth.
                • 

              

              What it does not do
              

                

              • No sampler. The SAMPLER sound source cannot be chosen. A project that had a sampler track loads with the 808 kit on that track.
                • 

              • No DX7 operator editing on the device. The DX7 quick page stays (preset, bank, ALGORITHM, FEEDBACK, TRANSPOSE, LEVEL). Voices are edited and imported in the workbench. Pressing PARA on another sound source, or SCALE, CHORD or KNOB BANK+CHORD outside the song pages, shows VOICE EDIT MOVED TO WORKBENCH.
                • 

              • No Bluetooth page and no project NAME page on the device. Both moved to the workbench.
                • 

              • No factory scenes. The preset list shows the 16 USER project slots only.
                • 

              

              The built-in synth is a preview
              

              The SMK-37 keeps five sound sources: DX7 FM (called FM6 in the documentation), BASS 303, DRUM 808, PSG and PLUCK. In a song they are there to audition a part before it goes to external gear, or to play a part when no gear is on that channel. Which tracks sound inside and which go out is set per track with the SEQ setting on the MIDI TRACK page. Chapter 09 explains it.
              

              Where to see the installed version
              

                

              • Boot screen: the line under OFFICIAL OPEN shows the version, for example TABBY-V04.14. The screen font has capitals only.
                • 

              • Workbench: the badge next to the title shows the same version.
                • 

              • Device update tab: the Version line shows it. Firmware details also show the build ID and the Open base version, which stays V01.
                • 

              

              

              02 · Getting started
              

              Back up first
              

              Before you install, keep what you want to keep. In Projects & sounds, under Device projects, load each slot you care about and click Back up current project. Under Song mode, read each song and click Export .tabby. Songs are the one thing a factory V16 restore overwrites in part, so keep the .tabby files.
              

              Install
              

                

              1. Open the Classic Tabby workbench in desktop Chrome or Edge. Use the hosted page or the SMK37-Open-Source.html file from the release.
                2. 

              2. Open the Device update tab. The page shows Firmware SMK37 Pro Open and the version. Check that the version is the one you downloaded.
                3. 

              3. Connect the SMK-37 Pro by USB. Tick the back-up box. Click Connect device and allow MIDI with SysEx.
                4. 

              4. Read the identity line. SMK-37 Pro_8000001 is an Open firmware. SMK-37 Pro_016 is the factory firmware. Anything else is not this device, so stop.
                5. 

              5. From an Open firmware, click Start update. From the factory firmware, open Migration, factory restore and forced updates, tick Force flash, wait for the page to reconnect, confirm the warning, then Start update. If the device does not answer, power-cycle it and connect again; never use force flash on an Open firmware.
                6. 

              6. Keep power and USB connected until the page reports the restart and the version check.
                7. 

              

              Songs written by tabby-v02.0 keep playing as before, including swing. Reflashing from tabby-v03.0 to tabby-v03.1 is optional. Both have the same sequencer.
              

              First boot
              

              The boot screen shows SMK37, OFFICIAL OPEN and the version. When song storage holds data that is not in the song format (V01's sample bank or DX7 library, or what the tabby-v04.0 storage move left), the device shows OLD DATA - SEE ACTIONS for six seconds. Until it is erased, the SONG page says OLD DATA IN SONG STORAGE and no song can be written or played. The workbench says the same when it connects the project library.
              

              To erase it: press SEQ and PARA together to open the ACTIONS menu, turn K5 or K1 to ERASE OLD DATA and press > (after KNOB BANK, FADER BANK, PATCH); the screen asks ERASE OLD DATA? and a second > (after KNOB BANK, FADER BANK, PATCH) confirms (PATCH cancels). The workbench's Erase old data… does the same after its own confirmation. The erase runs one sector per control cycle and dips the audio briefly if something plays. Projects, tunings and settings are not touched. Afterwards the SONG page says NO SONG HERE - UPLOAD FROM THE WEB WORKBENCH and the storage status reports 326080 bytes free.
              


              Connect the workbench
              

              Open Projects & sounds and click Connect project library. The page reads the device's capabilities. The Song mode group becomes usable with the device as the target, and the Bluetooth settings group appears. Everything in this tab talks to the device over USB MIDI. Close other MIDI software first if the connection fails.
              

              The Play & edit tab has shortcuts into the simulator's pages. Song mode opens the SONG page and Track launch opens the CLIPS page in the browser simulator, which runs the same firmware code.
              

              

              03 · Songs
              

              Clips and scenes
              

              On the device a song is clips and scenes. Each of the 8 tracks has up to 64 clips. A scene names one clip (or nothing) for each track, how many times it plays, and whether the next scene follows by itself. The scenes in order are the song. Chapter 05 covers everything you do with them on the panel: launching, editing, recording, chains, settings.
              

              The workbench's song editor shows the same song as rows and blocks: a row is a scene, a block is a clip. The rest of this chapter uses the editor's words.
              

              Every clip loops at its own length: a 1-bar clip in a 4-bar scene plays four times. A song you imported plays as it did, and a song saved on the device (after a new clip, a stored scene or a changed setting) is kept in the scenes format, which firmware before tabby-v04.10 cannot read.
              

              Rows, blocks, repeats, step lengths
              

              A song is a list of rows. A row names one block per track, eight ids in all. A block is a pattern of up to 64 steps with up to 4 notes per step. Block id 0 means the track is silent in that row. One block can appear in many rows and on many tracks, so a drum pattern used in 20 rows is stored once.
              

              Each row also has a repeat count from 1 to 64, a step length of 16, 32, 48 or 64 steps, and a Loop here flag. A row of 16 steps is one bar. The song plays the row's blocks for the row's length, then plays the row again for each repeat, then moves to the next row. A row with Loop here repeats until you jump away.
              

              The song header holds the name (12 characters), a tempo override (0 keeps the project tempo), the Loop the song flag with its Loop start row, the jump landing rule (next bar or end of row), the swing flag, and an output channel per track (0 keeps the device OUT CH of that track).
              

              What a song stores and what the project slot stores
              

              The song stores notes, rows, row events, output channels and the tempo override. The project stores sounds, mixer levels, swing, the clock source and the per-track MIDI settings (IN CH, OUT CH, SEQ, OUT PORT). A song plays with whatever project is loaded on the device. The song's project slot field is only a note of the project it was made for. The device does not load that project for you. Load the project on the overview first, then start the song.
              

              The device holds 16 songs in its song storage, the flash area that used to hold samples. The workbench's Song mode group reads, writes, deletes and exports them. From tabby-v04.8 the device edits songs too (chapter 05); it saves only while the song is stopped.
              

              Playing a song on the device
              

                

              1. Press SEQ and PARA together to open ACTIONS.
                2. 

              2. Turn K5 or K1 to SONG MODE and press > (after KNOB BANK, FADER BANK, PATCH). The SONG page opens.
                3. 

              3. Turn K5 or K7 to choose song 1 to 16. This works while the song is stopped.
                4. 

              4. Press SEQ PLAY. The song starts at row 1. If the project's pattern sequencer was running it stops. Press SEQ PLAY again to stop. Every note is released and MIDI Stop is sent once.
                5. 

              5. PATCH leaves the page. The song keeps playing.
                6. 

              

              In the browser simulator the Song mode shortcut on the Play & edit tab opens the same page.
              

              Every line on the SONG page
              

              LineMeaning
              

              Top lineOn every page, large: the tempo, PLAY / STOP / PAUS / REC / ARMD (record armed) / CNT4 (count-in), and the selected track. Small, on the right: ARP, K8=0 while the master volume is at zero, CPU! while the CPU guard takes voices back (from tabby-v1.2 this is a mark, not a message), and in amber *SNG (a clip or the song waits for a save), *PRJ (the project does) or *S+P.
              

              SONG nLarge: the selected song slot. Under it its name and, when the song sets its own tempo, BPM n.
              

              OLD DATALarge, in amber: song storage is blocked by V01 data. Erase it from ACTIONS. Also possible: STORAGE ERROR, COMPACTING, SCANNING.
              

              SCENE r / totalLarge: the scene (row) playing and the number of scenes in the song.
              

              NEXT n, LOOPING, LAST SCENE, STOPPEDLarge: what follows the current scene when nothing is queued: the next scene, the same scene (Loop here), or nothing because the song ends. With Loop the song on, the last scene is followed by the loop start.
              

              TO nLarge, in amber, in the same place: a scene recall is queued and lands at the next master cycle or the end of the scene. AT n: the scene reserved while stopped.
              

              TOO MANY BLKS, BLOCK RD ERROR, DECODE LATELarge, in amber, in the same place: the song has more than 2048 blocks and will not play; a block could not be read, so that track is silent in that scene; a scene was not decoded in time and the previous one played again.
              

              X pass / passes, BAR b / barsWhich pass of the scene is playing and how many it has; the bar inside the scene and how many bars it has.
              

              LT mIn amber, on that line: scene entries whose events or notes came after the bar line since SEQ PLAY. Chapter 05 and chapter 08 say when that happens.
              

              Eight numbers in the tracks' coloursThe clip each track plays in the shown scene. -- is silence.
              

              Two rows of eight cellsThe 16 scenes the pads reach, laid out like the pads, each with its number (the last two digits): green plays, amber is queued or reserved, grey exists, dark is no scene. OCTAVE- and OCTAVE+ turn the page in steps of 16.
              

              TIME, THEN, HOLD, JUMPK1 to K4: how many times the scene plays; what follows it (STAY, NEXT, LOOP, END); HELD or RUN (the chain's hold); where a queued scene recall lands: CYC, the next master cycle (one bar unless the song says otherwise), or END, the end of the scene that plays. The jump choice is saved in the song.
              

              NO SONG HERELarge, in amber: the slot is empty. Write a song from the workbench or make one with ACTIONS: NEW SONG.
              

              

              From tabby-v1.1 nothing on the screen is smaller than 10 x 14 pixels a character, and what you need on stage is half as large again. The key help that used to stand at the bottom of the pages is in this Help and in the guide. A message such as NO SUCH SCENE / NOT PLAYING is an amber box across the top of the screen for a moment (over the top line, from tabby-v1.2; it does not cover the pads' cells; from tabby-v1.2.1 PLAY / STOP stays at its left end and any press takes it away), in large black letters on one to three lines.
              

              How the song ends
              

              With Loop the song off, the song stops after the last row, releases every note and sends MIDI Stop. With Loop the song on it continues from the Loop start row. When tracks are detached by a launch (chapter 05) the song does not stop at its end. The following tracks go silent, the page shows SONG OVER, the launched tracks keep looping and the clock keeps running until you press SEQ PLAY.
              

              The song editor in the workbench
              

              In Projects & sounds, open Song mode (Classic Tabby). Choose the Target: Device (project library) or Browser simulator. Choose the Song slot. Read song loads the slot into the editor. New song starts an empty one. The editor shows the name, project slot, BPM, the loop boxes, the loop start row, where jumps land, the output channels, the row table (one line per row with the eight block ids, Repeat, Steps and Loop here), Add row and Remove last row, the row events, and the block editor. Write song writes the song record first, then every block in the editor in batches, then reads the record back and compares. Delete song clears the slot. Storage status asks the device how much room is left.
              

              Writing to a slot that already holds a song deletes the old song first. The page says so and suggests an Export .tabby of the old song before you confirm.
              

              

              04 · Scene changes
              

              A scene change is a jump to another row while the song plays. You queue it from the pads of the SONG page.
              

                

              1. On the SONG page, read PADS a - b. Pad 1 is scene (row) a, pad 16 is scene b. OCTAVE- and OCTAVE+ move the window by 16 rows, up to row 128.
                2. 

              2. Press the pad of the row you want. The page shows TO SCENE n in amber at once, and the pad blinks green.
                3. 

              3. The jump lands on the next master cycle when JUMP: NEXT CYCLE is shown, or when the current scene has played all its repeats when JUMP: SCENE END is shown. K4 switches between the two. The setting is saved in the song as Jumps land at.
                4. 

              4. At the landing the page shows SCENE n and X 1, every track starts the new row's blocks together, and the new row's events have been sent before its first notes.
                5. 

              

              What to expect
              

                

              • Press several pads inside one bar and only the last one lands. Press the same pad ten times and one jump lands.
                • 

              • A pad with no row behind it, or a press while the song is stopped, shows NO SUCH SCENE / NOT PLAYING and queues nothing.
                • 

              • A jump cancels every pending track launch, stop and return (chapter 05) and brings every launched or stopped track back to the song at the landing. Notes of launched tracks are released at the landing.
                • 

              • A jump queued inside the last half step before the bar can land with its notes and events a little late. LATE counts up by one on the page.
                • 

              • From tabby-v04.7 the pads light on the SONG page: off for no scene, dim white for a scene, green for the scene that plays, blinking green for the scene that is queued.
                • 

              • A row with Loop here never moves on by itself. Use a jump to leave it.
                • 

              

              

              05 · Clip launching
              

              Clip launching lets one track leave the scenes and loop one of its clips while the other tracks keep following the song. A clip is one pattern of one track. Each track has its own list of clips, up to 64, in numbered places; a scene (a row of the song) names one clip per track. The complete list of controls is in docs/CONTROL-MAP.md of the source.
              

              The CLIPS page
              

              Press BT on any page. The CLIPS page opens; BT again returns to the page you came from. From the SONG page SCALE also opens it, and SCALE on the CLIPS page goes to the SONG page. PATCH leaves to the overview. The page shows:
              

                

              • CLIPS and BAR n, the bar counter since SEQ PLAY. The selected track, the tempo and PLAY / STOP / REC are in the top line, large.
                • 

              • S n SCENE n, large: the song slot and the song's current scene. In amber instead: NO SONG HERE, OLD DATA, STORAGE ERROR.
                • 

              • One cell per track, in two rows of four: the track's number in its colour (in a filled box for the selected track) and, large, the place of the clip it plays: white when it follows the scenes, green when it loops a launched clip, -- when it is stopped, amber or blue when the track is muted. Under it, large: >05 in amber means the clip in place 5 is queued, >ST a queued stop, >SC a return to the scenes at the next master cycle; +05 or +ST in green is where the clip's chain leads; MUT (amber) or INT (blue) marks a muted track.
                • 

              • Two rows of eight cells, laid out like the pads: the 16 places of the selected track's pad bank. A numbered cell is a clip. A green cell is the one playing, an amber cell the one queued, a dark cell no clip, a framed cell the selected clip. OCTAVE- and OCTAVE+ change the bank.
                • 

              • At the bottom, only when there is something to say: SONG OVER when the song has ended with detached tracks, and LATE n.
                • 

              • SEQ PLAY starts and stops the song here as on the SONG page.
                • 

              

              Selecting a track
              

              Hold KNOB BANK and press pad 1 to 8, or turn K5. The pads show the track colours while KNOB BANK is held: dim for a track at rest, bright for a track with a clip playing, flashing for a track with something queued, and one level brighter for the selected track. Pads 9 to 16 mute and unmute tracks 1 to 8 under KNOB BANK.
              

              Launching a clip
              

              Press the pad of a clip. The pad blinks green, the column shows > n and the notice says LAUNCH AT NEXT CYCLE. At the next master cycle the clip starts, the pad turns steady green and the column shows CLIP. If the track was playing another clip, that clip's notes are released at the cycle. A second pad inside the same cycle replaces the queued clip. The launched clip loops with its own length, so a 48-step clip against 16-step scenes lines up again every three bars. The pad you pressed is also the selected clip.
              

              The master cycle is one bar (16 steps) unless the song says otherwise; a song imported from a 3/4 file has a cycle of 12 steps. Launches, stops, returns and scene recalls all land on its multiples, counted from SEQ PLAY.
              

              Stopping a track
              

              Press the green pad, the clip that plays. It blinks red, the track's cell shows >ST and the notice says STOP AT NEXT CYCLE. At the cycle every note of the track gets its note-off on the channel it was sent on, the pad goes white and the cell shows --. A stopped track stays silent until you launch a clip or send it back to the scenes. Stopping every track never stops the transport, the clock or the Song Position Pointer.
              

              Taking a press back, and selecting without launching
              

              Press a blinking pad again and its launch or stop is taken back (TAKEN BACK). Hold a pad for half a second and its clip is selected only: what the press queued is taken back (SELECTED ONLY - TAKEN BACK). While the song is stopped a pad reserves its clip, as on the MC-707: the pad blinks, the notice says RESERVED FOR SEQ PLAY, and SEQ PLAY starts the song with that track on the reserved clip while the other tracks follow scene 1. Press the blinking pad again to take the reservation back. (With CLOCK on MIDI the song starts on its scenes.)
              

              Back to the scenes
              

              CHORD queues the selected track back to the scenes: the column shows >SCN and the notice TO SCENES AT CYCLE. At the next cycle the track joins the scene the song is in at that moment and shows SCENE. KNOB BANK+CHORD does it for every track at once (ALL TO SCENES AT CYCLE). With the song stopped the notice says NOT PLAYING.
              

              Mute
              

              KNOB BANK + pad 9 to 16 mutes track 1 to 8: the internal sound is silenced and, from tabby-v04.7, the track's song notes are held back on MIDI out too. The clip runs on, so unmuting brings it back in time. The notice says TRACK MUTED - SOUND + MIDI. The pads of such a track are orange, the CLIPS page shows MUT in amber under the track and the overview MUTE. A mute set on the mixer page, and the mute that tracks 6 and 7 of a new project start with, silence the internal sound only, as before: the song still plays those tracks on MIDI out. That mute looks different: blue pads, INT in blue on the CLIPS page and on the overview. With KNOB BANK held, pads 9 to 16 are orange, blue or dim green for the eight tracks. KNOB BANK + pad on a muted track of either kind unmutes it.
              

              Banks and messages
              

              OCTAVE- and OCTAVE+ (or K6) turn the pad bank in steps of 16 clips, four banks. The messages are: RESERVED FOR SEQ PLAY when the song is stopped, NO CLIP ON THIS PAD when the place is empty, LAUNCH AT NEXT CYCLE and STOP AT NEXT CYCLE when a queue was taken, TAKEN BACK when one was withdrawn.
              

              Pad colours and flashing
              

              PadMeaning
              

              OffEmpty: no clip of the selected track in that place.
              

              Dim whiteStopped: a clip that is not playing.
              

              Steady greenThe clip that plays.
              

              Blinking greenThe clip queued to start at the next master cycle.
              

              Blinking redThe playing clip, with a stop queued.
              

              Bright white / bright greenThe selected clip, not playing / playing.
              

              OrangeThe track is muted altogether (sound and song notes): dim for a clip that is not playing, bright for the one that plays.
              

              BlueOnly the track's internal sound is muted (a mixer mute); the song still plays it on MIDI out. Dim and bright as for orange.
              

              Track colours (with KNOB BANK)Pads 1 to 8 are the tracks. Dim at rest, bright while a clip plays, flashing while something is queued, brighter for the selected track.
              

              

              While the song runs the blinking follows the master clock, one change per eighth note. With the song stopped the pads blink every quarter second.
              

              Scenes and launched tracks
              

                

              • A scene recall on the SONG page overrides everything queued on the CLIPS page and brings every track back to the scenes at the landing.
                • 

              • A launched or stopped track ignores row changes until it returns.
                • 

              • When the song's last row ends and no track is detached, the usual song end applies. When a track is detached, the following tracks go silent, SONG OVER appears, the detached tracks keep looping and the clock keeps running. SEQ PLAY stops everything and sends MIDI Stop.
                • 

              • Every launch, stop and return lands on the next master cycle (a bar of 16 steps unless the song says otherwise), whatever the scene lengths.
                • 

              • A press inside the last control cycle before the bar cannot be served on that bar. The pattern enters at the next cycle in phase, its downbeat skipped, and LATE counts up by one.
                • 

              • A launch sends the program change of the clip's scene for the track's channel, Lead ms before the cycle (chapter 08). A clip that no scene uses has no scene events; a v3 clip's own program and bank are sent with its first note.
                • 

              

              The step loop (tabby-v04.23)
              

              While the song plays, on CLIPS, hold NOTE REPEAT: pads 9 to 12 light amber and pads 13 to 16 go dark. Hold pad 9, 10, 11 or 12 and every track that plays repeats its last 1, 2, 4 or 8 steps (16th notes of what it plays) until the pad is let go: STEP LOOP: LAST 4 STEPS, then STEP LOOP OFF. The clocks run on underneath: clips, chains, scenes and the master cycle change as they would, and the song continues where it would have been. The loop takes the steps that end with the step each track is in when the pad goes down. A loop is not longer than the clip that plays. While NOTE REPEAT is down no pad launches a clip. Refused while the song is stopped (STEP LOOP - PLAY FIRST) and during a take (NOT DURING A TAKE).
              

              Editing a clip: the STEP page (tabby-v04.8)
              

              Select a clip on the CLIPS page (its pad is bright; hold a pad for half a second to select it without launching) and press PARA. The STEP page opens on that clip; with none selected it opens on the clip the track plays. PARA again returns to CLIPS and keeps the clip open. As on the MC-707, one set of controls chooses the step and another enters the notes: here the 16 pads are the steps of one bar and the keyboard enters the notes.
              

              ControlWhat it does
              

              PadSelects its step and lists the step's notes. The same pad again deselects it.
              

              A key, with a step selectedEnters that note on the step with the velocity you played, one step long (NOTE ENTERED). The same key again removes it (NOTE REMOVED). Several keys make a chord. The key sounds as always.
              

              A key, with no step selectedBecomes the current note, shown as NOTE.
              

              SCALESwitches the pads between PADS SELECT A STEP and PADS TOGGLE: in TOGGLE a pad puts the current note on its step or takes it off, one press per drum hit. The page opens in TOGGLE on a drum track.
              

              K1 / K2 / K3 / K4Choose a note of the selected step (the > mark) / its velocity / its start, up to half a step early or late in units of 1/480 step / its length.
              

              K5 / K7The current note by semitones / the selected step's probability.
              

              OCTAVE- / OCTAVE+ or K6The previous / next bar of 16 steps.
              

              CHORD / KNOB BANK+CHORDClear the selected step / discard every unsaved change and return to CLIPS.
              

              FX / KNOB BANK+FXUndo, four levels / redo.
              

              >Save the clip into the song. Only while the song is stopped; while it plays the notice says STOP TO SAVE.
              

              SEQ PLAYStart and stop the song.
              

              

              The pads: off for an empty step, dim white for an empty step on a beat, green for a step with notes, amber for a step that holds the current note, cyan for the selected step, white for the step that plays now.
              

                

              • While the clip is unsaved the top line shows *SNG in amber. Nothing is written to flash while a song plays. An unsaved clip is saved with > while stopped, by itself ten seconds after the last change once the song is stopped (CLIP SAVED), or when you choose another song. Unsaved changes are lost at power-off.
                • 

              • The song plays the unsaved edit. A clip launched on its track plays each change from its next loop; a track that follows the scenes plays the changed clip the next time a scene brings it.
                • 

              • Eight clips can be unsaved at a time (from tabby-v1.3; one before). Open, record or make another clip while one is unsaved: the first waits, keeps playing as you left it, and is saved with the others when the song is stopped. Only the open clip has undo. A ninth is refused (8 UNSAVED - STOP TO SAVE).
                • 

              • A clip holds 512 events; one more is refused with CLIP FULL. A clip that two tracks share cannot be edited on the device (CLIP SHARED BY ANOTHER TRACK).
                • 

              • A saved clip is stored as a v3 clip and plays the same. A song edited on the device needs tabby-v04.5 or later to play, and the workbench of tabby-v04.5.1 or later to back up.
                • 

              

              Shifting a clip (tabby-v04.21): on the STEP page KNOB BANK+OCTAVE+ moves every note, controller and step probability of the clip one step later (CLIP SHIFTED ONE STEP LATER), KNOB BANK+OCTAVE- one step earlier. What leaves one end of the clip comes in at the other. A note keeps its place inside its step. A run of shifts is one undo level. Not during a take.
              

              Recording into a clip (tabby-v04.9)
              

              SEQ REC on the CLIPS page or the STEP page starts a take into the track's clip: the one open on the STEP page, else the selected one, else the one the track plays. What is in the clip stays; you add to it (overdub). The clip must loop on its track while you record, and SEQ REC sees to that.
              

                

              1. Select the clip (hold its pad on CLIPS), or open it on the STEP page.
                2. 

              2. Press SEQ REC. With the song playing and the clip looping the notice says RECORDING and the SEQ REC lamp lights. If the clip is not looping it is launched: REC WHEN THE CLIP LOOPS, and the take starts at the next master cycle. With the song stopped: REC ARMED - SEQ PLAY: GO; press SEQ PLAY. From tabby-v04.16, stopping the song before such a waiting take has started takes it off (SONG STOPPED - REC OFF); a take armed while stopped still waits for SEQ PLAY.
                3. 

              3. Play the keys or pads, or send notes from outside gear to MIDI in on the track's input channel. Each note is written when it ends and the clip plays it from its next loop.
                4. 

              4. Press SEQ REC again: REC STOPPED. The clip is unsaved (*SNG in the top line) and is saved as after a step edit (stopped: >, or by itself after ten seconds).
                5. 

              

                

              • Input quantize is on at power-up: a note is recorded on the nearest step, with the length you played. KNOB BANK+SEQ REC switches it off and on (INPUT QUANTIZE OFF / ON); off, a note keeps the time you played it. The STEP page shows Q ON or Q OFF.
                • 

              • Controllers below 120, pitch bend and channel pressure are recorded too, thinned: a moving controller once per 1/32 note, and its last value when it stops. A sweep does not fill the clip.
                • 

              • A take is one undo level: after the take, FX on the STEP page takes the whole take back. There is no undo during a take.
                • 

              • Clearing notes (tabby-v04.21): while a take runs, hold FX and hold a key. Each note of that key is taken out of the clip as the clip passes it; one pass of the clip clears them all. The key sounds but is not recorded; several keys can be held. During a take FX does nothing else (alone it says HOLD FX + A KEY: CLEARS ITS NOTES). Cleared notes come back with the undo of the take.
                • 

              • A clip holds 512 events. When it is full the take stops by itself: CLIP FULL - REC STOPPED, the SEQ REC lamp goes out, and the clip's pad on CLIPS shows red once. Nothing already recorded is lost.
                • 

              • The take also stops when the song stops, when another clip is launched on the track, at a scene recall, and when CHORD sends the track back to the scenes.
                • 

              • Not recorded: polyphonic aftertouch, program changes, controllers 120 to 127.
                • 

              • From tabby-v04.10 a take is placed one audio block (3 ms) earlier than before, where you heard it; a take without input quantize now plays back where you played it.
                • 

              

              A new song on the panel (tabby-v04.21)
              

              On SCENES, with the song stopped, turn K5 to a slot that shows NO SONG. Press SEQ+PARA for ACTIONS, choose NEW SONG and press >: NEW SONG IN SLOT nn? Press > again (PATCH cancels). The new song is stored at once and CLIPS opens: NEW SONG - HOLD A PAD, SEQ REC. It is named NEW SONG, uses the loaded project and its tempo, loops, and has one empty scene of 16 steps and a master cycle of 16 steps. Make clips on its empty pads, launch them and store scenes as below; delete the empty first scene when you have one of your own. A slot that holds a song is refused (SLOT HOLDS A SONG - K5 ON SCENES). The name is changed in the workbench's song editor.
              

              New clips, length and copies (tabby-v04.10)
              

                

              • A new clip. Press an empty pad on CLIPS: it is selected (dim cyan) and nothing is queued. SEQ REC then records a new clip there, and PARA opens a new empty clip on the STEP page. A new clip is one master cycle long.
                • 

              • CLIP SETTING. FX on the CLIPS page opens it on the selected clip (FX again returns). K5 chooses the row, K1 changes its value, K2 changes it in steps of 16.
                • 

              • LENGTH, 1 to 128 steps. A shorter clip loses the notes past its new end (NOTES PAST THE END REMOVED); FX on the STEP page brings them back. A longer clip gets empty steps.
                • 

              • COPY TO PAD. K1 chooses an empty pad of the same track; > makes the copy. The copy is open and unsaved. The clip you copy from may be unsaved too (from tabby-v1.3).
                • 

              • Every clip loops at its own length. A 1-bar clip in a 4-bar scene plays four times; a 4-bar clip in a 1-bar scene plays through. Songs you imported play as before.
                • 

              • Saving. New clips, copies, stored scenes and the settings below belong to the song. The top line shows *SNG until the song is saved: stopped, with >, or by itself ten seconds after the stop (SAVED).
                • 

              

              Clip chains (tabby-v04.11)
              

              A chain tells a track what to do when a clip has played. Set it per clip on CLIP SETTING, on the three lines after LENGTH; it is saved with the clip.
              

                

              • NEXT CLIP: STAY (no chain), STOP (the track stops) or a clip of the same track. K1 steps through STAY, STOP and the pads that hold a clip.
                • 

              • AFTER: CLIP END, or 1 to 512 steps. TIMES: 1 to 64. The chain is due after TIMES x AFTER (or TIMES x the clip).
                • 

              • A chain runs on a track that plays the clip launched: from its pad, reserved before SEQ PLAY, or reached through another chain. A track that follows the scenes ignores chains.
                • 

              • The CLIPS page shows under the track's clip where the chain leads: +05 for clip 5, +ST for a stop.
                • 

              • Notes that sound when the next clip starts play out their length. A pad press, CHORD or a scene recall takes the track out of the chain.
                • 

              

              A clip's program and bank; the controller knobs (tabby-v04.13)
              

                

              • PROGRAM (OFF, 1 to 128), BANK MSB (OFF, 0 to 127) and BANK LSB on CLIP SETTING, after TIMES: a bank select and a program change sent on the track's channel when the track enters the clip, before its first notes. They go to MIDI out only.
                • 

              • Changed while the clip loops, the new values go out once at its next loop.
                • 

              • On the CLIPS page K1 to K4 send controllers 74, 71, 1 and 11 for the selected track, two per click; the screen shows the value. A take (SEQ REC) records the movements into the clip, thinned like any controller, and the clip plays them back.
                • 

              • From tabby-v04.14 the four numbers belong to the song: K1 CC to K4 CC (the controller numbers) on pages 3/4 and 4/4 of CLIP SETTING, 0 to 127 each (K2 moves by 16). A song that was never set uses 74, 71, 1 and 11.
                • 

              

              The pages of CLIP SETTING (tabby-v04.14; three pages from tabby-v04.17)
              

                

              • From tabby-v1.1 the page shows eight lines at a time in large letters, on four pages. Page 1/4 holds the clip's lines: LENGTH, NEXT CLIP, AFTER, TIMES, PROGRAM, BANK MSB, BANK LSB, COPY TO PAD. Page 2/4 holds more of the clip: TRANSPOSE, SHUFFLE, PLAY QUANT (play quantize), STEP SIZE, DIRECTION, DELETE CLIP. Pages 3/4 and 4/4 hold the song's lines: COUNT-IN, CLICK, CLICK OUT, CLICK CH, CLICK NOTE, CLICK LEVEL, K1 CC to K4 CC (the knobs' controller numbers), EVENT LEAD. K5 walks through all of them and the page changes by itself.
                • 

              • SHUFFLE (tabby-v04.17): SONG, or the clip's own shuffle from 0% to 50%. Every second 16th step comes that much of a step late. SONG follows the song's swing as every clip did before; 0% plays the clip straight in a song that swings.
                • 

              • PLAY QUANT (play quantize, tabby-v04.17): OFF, 1/16, 1/8 or 1/4. When the clip plays, each note starts on the nearest line of that grid (a note exactly halfway goes to the earlier line). The notes stored in the clip keep their own timing, so OFF brings it back; controllers are not moved. A clip with a SHUFFLE or a PLAY QUANT is refused by firmware before tabby-v04.17.
                • 

              • STEP SIZE (tabby-v04.19): what one step of the clip lasts: 1/16 (as before), 1/8, 1/32, 16T or 8T (the triplet sizes 1/16T and 1/8T). A clip of 16 steps lasts two bars at 1/8 and half a bar at 1/32; a clip of 12 steps at 1/16T lasts half a bar, in triplets. K1 only stops at a size that gives the clip a whole number of 16ths from 1 to 128 (triplets need a length that divides by 3); the line shows the result in 16ths after the size, for example 1/8=032. The notes stored in the clip are not changed. The STEP page still shows the clip's own steps, and a take is recorded in them. A clip with a STEP SIZE other than 1/16 is refused by firmware before tabby-v04.19.
                • 

              • DIRECTION (tabby-v04.20): FORWARD, REVERSE or FWD+REV (forwards, then backwards). REVERSE plays the steps from the last to the first; a note keeps its place inside its step and its length. FWD+REV plays the clip forwards and then backwards and lasts twice as long; when that would pass 128 steps or 512 events the value ends in ! in amber and the clip plays forwards. The stored clip is not changed. The STEP page shows the clip's own steps: the running light walks backwards and a take is recorded where it is heard. A clip with a DIRECTION other than FORWARD is refused by firmware before tabby-v04.20.
                • 

              • EVENT LEAD (tabby-v1.0.2): OFF, 1/32, 1/16, 1/8 or 1/4: how long before a scene's downbeat its row events (program changes, bank select, controllers) are sent. OFF, the value of every song that never set it, sends them at the downbeat as before. With a lead the scene's first notes no longer wait behind those messages on a shared DIN cable (about 0.8 ms a message). The price: the synth changes its sound that much before the downbeat, so the tail of the previous scene's last notes is heard on the new sound; choose the shortest lead that is enough. A device's gap from the rig profile still counts from its own program change; the lead comes in front. No lead at SEQ PLAY (use SEND SETUP first). Heard from the scene after the next; saved with the song.
                • 

              • CLICK LEVEL: LOW, MID or HIGH for the internal click, each twice as loud as the one before. A song that was never set is on MID. The click as a MIDI note is not affected.
                • 

              

              Transpose and delete a clip (tabby-v04.15)
              

                

              • TRANSPOSE, -12 to +12 semitones: every note of the clip is moved when the clip plays. The notes stored in the clip stay, so 0 plays the clip as it was. Heard from the clip's next loop; saved with the clip.
                • 

              • DELETE CLIP: with the song stopped, press > (> AGAIN - DELETES THE CLIP) and press it again within two seconds (CLIP DELETED - SAVE THE SONG). A clip that a scene uses is not deleted; the screen says USED BY SCENE n. Until you save the song, loading it again brings the clip back.
                • 

              

              The scene chain (tabby-v04.12)
              

              The scenes of a song play in order. On the SCENES page three knobs set how, for the scene that plays (stopped: for the scene you reserved by pressing its pad).
              

                

              • K1: how many times the scene plays before the next one (1 to 64). The line LEN shows the scene's length in master cycles.
                • 

              • K2: THEN NEXT (the following scene comes by itself) or THEN STAY (the scene repeats until you recall another).
                • 

              • K3 (HOLD): HELD keeps the scene that plays, whatever its settings say; RUN lets the song go on. The hold is not stored.
                • 

              • A pad always wins: the song jumps to that scene and goes on from there.
                • 

              • While the song is stopped, a scene pad reserves the scene (RESERVED FOR SEQ PLAY) and SEQ PLAY starts there; the pad again takes it back.
                • 

              • The settings belong to the song: unsaved (*SNG) until saved.
                • 

              

              Click and count-in (tabby-v04.10)
              

              The lower rows of CLIP SETTING belong to the song and are stored with it. A song you never set has no click and no count-in.
              

                

              • COUNT-IN: OFF, 1, 2 or 4 master cycles. With a take armed (SEQ REC while stopped), SEQ PLAY clicks that long before the song starts; the CLIPS page shows COUNT-IN and the beats left. MIDI Start goes out when the song starts, after the count-in. The count-in always clicks, on the output chosen below.
                • 

              • CLICK: OFF, REC ONLY (while a take is armed or runs) or ALWAYS. A click on every quarter note, the first of a master cycle louder.
                • 

              • CLICK OUT: INTERNAL (a click on the audio output, after the master volume), MIDI (a note on MIDI out), or BOTH. If the SMK-37's audio goes to the house mix, use MIDI.
                • 

              • CLICK CH and CLICK NOTE: where the MIDI click goes. Channel 10, note 37 unless you change them.
                • 

              

              Storing a scene (tabby-v04.10)
              

              On the SCENES page, while the song plays, hold an empty pad for half a second: what plays now becomes a new scene after the last one (STORED AS A NEW SCENE): for each track the clip it plays, nothing for a stopped track. The scene repeats until you recall another one. A pad that holds a scene is never written over; holding it recalls it like a short press.
              

              Deleting and moving a scene (tabby-v04.16)
              

              With the song stopped, the selected scene on SCENES is the one whose pad blinks (press its pad), or scene 1. FX asks FX AGAIN DELETES SCENE and its number; FX again within two seconds deletes it (SCENE DELETED - SAVE THE SONG). The later scenes move one pad earlier and the scene's clips stay in the song. Hold PARA and turn K1 to move the selected scene one pad earlier or later (SCENE MOVED - SAVE THE SONG); it stays selected. A scene stored while playing is added after the last one: stop and move it to its place. A song keeps at least one scene. There is no undo for a deleted scene (the song is saved by the >, by itself ten seconds after the change, or when you choose another song); its clips stay, so it can be stored again. In an imported song a change that would alter the length of a clip is refused (KEPT - IT SETS A CLIP'S LENGTH): turn that clip's LENGTH one step and back on CLIP SETTING and save, then try again. Save with >.
              

              

              06 · Importing MIDI files
              

              The panel Import MIDI file (Classic Tabby) in Projects & sounds turns a Standard MIDI File (type 0 or 1, including Renoise exports and mf2t text) into a song. Everything happens in the browser. Nothing is sent until step 6.
              

              Step by step
              

                

              1. 1. MIDI file. Choose the .mid file. The summary shows the format, ticks per quarter note, tracks, parts, bars, the meter and the tempo. File warnings appear under it.
                2. 

              2. 2. Parts to Classic Tabby tracks. Every MIDI track and channel is a part. The table shows its name, channel, note count, range, bars and the program changes it contains. Assign each part to track 1 to 8 or skip it. Several parts may share a track; the 4-notes-per-step limit then applies to the mix. Drum parts on channel 10 are marked. Under the table, OUT CH per track sets the output channel written into the song header; device keeps the device's OUT CH for that track.
                3. 

              3. 3. Options. Bars from and to cut the range. Bars per row offers only lengths that stay on bar lines. Row events chooses the pre-roll for program changes and CCs (one beat before, at the row start only, or up to one bar before). Quantize is off by default (exact timing); it can snap note starts, or starts and ends, to 16ths, and then Note ends picks the rounding rule. More than 4 notes on a step keeps the 4 loudest, highest or lowest. Then the song name, the project slot, loop the whole song, and loose block matching with its velocity tolerance.
                4. 

              4. 4. Resulting song. The statistics line and the row table, then Dropped or changed: the warning list.
                5. 

              5. 5. Browser song. Save song (JSON) keeps the model on your computer. Export .tabby file writes the device file format. Load song JSON brings a saved model back.
                6. 

              6. 6. Write to the device or the simulator. Choose the Song slot, read what the slot holds, click Write song… and confirm. The target follows the Target choice of the Song mode group above (device or browser simulator). The panel then shows the batch plan and the time taken.
                7. 

              

              Track assignment and output channels
              

              The first eight non-empty parts are pre-assigned to tracks 1 to 8. A part's notes are stored in the row and step where they start. A note is anchored to the nearest 16th step and keeps its offset and length, so a part keeps its feel. OUT CH per track decides which channel the device sends that track on while the song plays. Set it to the channel of the gear that should play the part, or leave device to use the SEQ page setting.
              

              Exact timing and the quantize option
              

              Timing is kept to 1/480 of a 16th step. Files with 96, 120, 192, 240, 384, 480, 960 or 1920 ticks per quarter note convert exactly. Other resolutions round to the nearest unit and the panel reports the largest rounding. Quantize snaps starts to the grid, or starts and ends, and only then the rules for note ends apply.
              

              The warnings and what each one means
              

              WarningMeaning
              

              The file has no tempo event; 120 BPM is usedThe song tempo is 120.
              

              Tempo … rounded, Tempo … clampedThe first tempo became an integer BPM, or was limited to 30 to 300.
              

              Tempo changes ignoredLater tempo events are dropped. The song keeps the first tempo.
              

              Time signature changes ignoredRows follow the first signature.
              

              No row length of 16/32/48/64 steps holds whole bars of …Meters such as 5/4 or 7/8 do not fit a row length. Rows are 64 steps and bar lines fall inside rows.
              

              Note starts moved to the 16th grid, Note lengths rounded to whole stepsOnly with Quantize on.
              

              Notes shorter than a step got length 1Only with Quantize on. With exact timing short notes keep their length.
              

              Notes outside bars …, Notes ending after bar …Notes outside the bar range were dropped or clipped at its end.
              

              Notes longer than … , Notes longer than 136 steps are stored to within the exponent scaleVery long notes are clipped, or stored with a coarser length step.
              

              The file's … ticks per quarter note do not divide 1920Note times were rounded to the nearest 1/480 step. The largest rounding is given in units and milliseconds.
              

              Same pitch twice on one step on one track; the quieter note was droppedTwo notes of the same pitch cannot share a step on a track.
              

              Same pitch overlapping on one track; the earlier note was shortenedA repeated pitch ends where the next one starts.
              

              More than 4 notes on one step on one track; kept the 4 …The overflow rule chose which four stay.
