              Blocks merged by loose matchingLoose matching reused a block whose velocities differ within the tolerance.
              

              Program / bank / control change event(s) at row starts became row eventsThey fire when the row starts. Everything else of that kind is listed as dropped.
              

              More than 32 events at one row startThe extra events were dropped.
              

              Bank select without a following program change droppedA bank select needs a program change after it.
              

              … control change, pitch bend, aftertouch, SysEx, other meta event(s) ignoredCounted and dropped. Sustain pedal is counted separately and not applied.
              

              MIDI parts not assigned to a track were skippedParts set to skip in step 2.
              

              

              Each warning shows a count and, where it applies, a positions list with the track and the bar.
              

              Deduplication
              

              Identical cells (the same notes, velocities, offsets and lengths) become one block id. Rows that repeat the same eight ids merge into one row with a repeat count. The merge loses nothing. Loose block matching also merges cells whose only difference is velocity, within the tolerance you set, and lists every merge.
              

              Writing and replacing a song
              

              Writing uses the song editor's path: an occupied slot is deleted first, then the song record goes, then the blocks in batches, then the record is read back and compared. The old song's blocks are reclaimed at the next compaction. Export a .tabby of the old song first if you want to keep it. Projects are never changed by a song write.
              

              

              07 · Timed notes
              

              Offsets and lengths
              

              Every note in a block carries a start offset and a length in units of 1/480 of a 16th step. The offset says how far before or after its step the note starts, from −240 to +240 units, which is half a step either way. A note belongs to the step nearest its start. The length is exact up to 65535 units, which is 8.5 bars of 4/4. The units are musical, so they scale with the tempo. At 120 BPM one unit is about 0.26 ms and one step is 125 ms.
              

              Reading them in the song editor
              

              In the block editor each step is a text field: pitch:velocity:length/offset. The length is in steps and may have decimals. The offset is in signed units. A trailing r means retrigger, @n a probability of n out of 8, and ! the alternate tuning. For example 60:100:1.5/-20 is a C4 at velocity 100, one and a half steps long, starting 20 units early. A step with an offset or a fractional length has an orange mark on its left.
              

              Editing them
              

              Click a step to open the inspector under the grid. It lists each note with its pitch, velocity, retrigger, offset (in units, with the fraction of a step and the milliseconds at the song's tempo) and length (steps and units). Change a value and the readouts follow. Quantize starts to 16ths clears every offset in the block. Quantize starts and ends to 16ths also rounds every length to whole steps. Store block keeps the edited block in the editor and Write song sends it to the device.
              

              Swing and old songs
              

              Songs written by tabby-v02.0 keep playing exactly as before, project swing included. When you write such a song again from the workbench it is stored in the new format and plays straight, whatever the project swing. Tick Swing follows the project setting in the song editor and write it again to make it swing. The swing itself is the project's SWING setting on the SYNC / MIDI page (SEQ, K3).
              

              

              08 · Program changes and CCs
              

              A row can carry events: program changes, bank selects and control changes. They fire when the row is entered, before the row's first notes, on every MIDI out port, addressed to a MIDI channel. The gear on that channel is described in the rig setup, so the editor can show preset names instead of numbers.
              

              The rig setup table
              

              In Projects & sounds open Rig setup (Classic Tabby). The table has one line per MIDI channel: Device (from the device library), Name (your name for it), Gap ms, Lead ms, Numbering (how the device counts programs and banks) and Names… for your own program names. Profile name, Export rig (.json), Import rig and Reset are above the table. The profile is saved in this browser. A song can carry its own copy of the rig; the row event editor has a box for that, and the copy travels in the .tabby file.
              

                

              • Gap ms is the pause the device needs after a program change or bank select. Blank uses the device definition. The gap becomes gap events in the song when it is written, so the device pre-fires the stream early enough for the last message to leave before the bar.
                • 

              • Lead ms makes the program change leave that long before the bar. It applies to track launches and scene changes alike. 0 sends it with the downbeat. Use it for gear that takes time to switch.
                • 

              

              The device library
              

              The library has definitions for the E-MU Proteus/2 XR, Eventide H90 Harmonizer, Zoom MS-70CDR+, Waldorf Blofeld, Waldorf Pulse 2, Dirtywave M8 Tracker Model:02, Korg volca fm2, Instruo Seashell and the M-VAVE FM-1 under the Skiff, Melodee and Orange Cat firmwares. Each one gives the program numbering, the bank scheme, named controllers and the preset names the manufacturer publishes. Unverified fields are marked and shown in the editor.
              

              Row events in the song editor
              

              Below the row table of the song editor, the Row selector picks a row. Row 1 is marked SEND SETUP because its events are the set-up list. The list shows each event with its channel, the device on it and the event in words. Arrows move an event, ✕ deletes it. Add on channel and type add a Program (from the preset list, with a bank where the device has banks, or a raw number), a Control change (named or raw, with the value meaning where known) or a Gap in ms. A row holds up to 32 events and a song up to 292. Gaps read back from the device are shown greyed and regenerated from the rig at the next write.
              

              SEND SETUP
              

              With the song loaded and stopped, open ACTIONS, choose SEND SETUP and press > (after KNOB BANK, FADER BANK, PATCH). Row 1's events go out at once and the notice says SETUP SENT - ROW 1 EVENTS. Use it before a set, after a power-up, and before SEQ PLAY on a song whose first row has gaps. With the song playing it says STOP THE SONG FIRST. With no song loaded it says NO SONG LOADED.
              

              What goes out when
              

                

              • A row change or a scene change sends the new row's events for every channel, with their gaps, pre-fired so the last message leaves before the bar.
                • 

              • A track launch or a return to the song sends only the events of the pattern's row that address that track's channel, Lead ms before the bar. Two tracks on one channel each send their own.
                • 

              • LATE on the SONG page counts rows whose stream ended after the bar line, for example SEQ PLAY on a row with gaps without SEND SETUP first, or a jump queued with less time left than the gaps need.
                • 

              • Events reach external gear only. The SMK-37's own presets are set by the project, not by events.
                • 

              

              Device setup checklist
              

              Without these settings on the gear itself, row events do nothing.
              

              DeviceSet on the device
              

              E-MU Proteus/2 XRMaster menu MIDI MODE = Multi. Per channel, MIDI ENABLE on and PRESET CHANGE on for every channel a song addresses. MIDI PROG>PRESET map: identity for presets 0 to 127, and an explicit mapping for any preset above 127, because the Proteus has no bank select. Leave the Edit menu, where program changes are ignored. Run SEND SETUP before SEQ PLAY.
              

              Eventide H90System > MIDI: the channel (15) or Receive Omni. PC Offset 0 or 1, and the rig profile set to match. The Playlist is the User List the program numbers refer to. Assign the CC numbers for bypass, HotSwitch and tap in Global Control and enter them in the rig. On firmware 1.8.6 to 1.9.x put the device gap after the program change.
              

              Zoom MS-70CDR+MENU > USB MIDI CH = 16 or OMNI. USB host powered and connected before the set. Patches 001 to 100 by program change only. Send PC 0 and PC 1 once and note which patch the display shows, to settle the base.
              

              Waldorf BlofeldGlobal MIDI Channel, or the part channel in Multi mode with the part's Prg Change filter on receive. Ctrl Receive = on, or no CC changes anything. Banks by CC 32 = 0 to 7 (A to H). Avoid channel 10 in Multi mode. Allow a gap after a program change.
              

              Waldorf Pulse 2Global MIDI Channel. Banks by CC 32 = 0 to 4. PC is clamped to 0 to 99 inside the bank. Program 500 is the random patch.
              

              Dirtywave M8 Model:02MIDI Settings: track channels, PG CHANGE = on. A program change selects the track's instrument (INST 00 to 7F). These settings are stored in the M8 song file.
              

              Korg volca fm2MIDI channel (hold MEMORY at power-on, key 1 to 16). Global 7 MIDI ShortMessage = on. No program change at all; a song can only send its CCs.
              

              Instruo SeashellMIDI channel in the Seashell Controller app. No program change in firmware 1.0.x; parameters by MIDI Learn only.
              

              

              

              09 · FM6 preview
              

              Each track decides where its notes go. The setting lives on the MIDI TRACK page, opened with KNOB BANK+SEQ from any page. K5 picks the track.
              

              KnobSetting
              

              K1 IN CHThe channel the track listens to from USB or Bluetooth MIDI.
              

              K2 OUT CHThe channel the track sends on. A song's output channel for the track overrides it while the song plays and is withdrawn when playback stops.
              

              K3 SEQLOCAL: the track's notes play the built-in sound only. BOTH: the built-in sound and MIDI out. MIDI: MIDI out only.
              

              K4 OUT PORTALL sends on every port (USB, Bluetooth, DIN). OFF sends nothing from this track.
              

              

              The SYNC / MIDI page (SEQ from any page) holds the global switches: K4 SEQ OUT (OFF, ON, CLOCK) and K7 KEY OUT. Song notes follow the same rules as pattern notes. Keep SEQ OUT on ON for notes and clock, or CLOCK for the clock alone.
              

              Audition a part, then hand it to the gear
              

                

              1. Give the track a built-in sound: FM6 (DX7 FM) or one of the others, chosen with KNOB BANK+PATCH, K1 or a pad, then > (after KNOB BANK, FADER BANK, PATCH).
                2. 

              2. Set its SEQ to LOCAL or BOTH and play the song. You hear the part on the SMK-37.
                3. 

              3. Set OUT CH to the channel of the external synth, or set the song's output channel for the track in the song editor.
                4. 

              4. Set SEQ to MIDI. The part now plays on the gear only. Set it back to BOTH to hear both.
                5. 

              

              Timing: MIDI out leaves in the audio block that holds the note's time. The built-in engine is one block looser, about 3 ms. The MIDI TRACK page's OUT CH readout shows the device setting even while a song overrides it. The project saves these settings; the song saves only its channel overrides.
              

              

              10 · Bluetooth settings
              

              The device no longer has a Bluetooth page. From tabby-v04.7 BT opens the CLIPS page (chapter 05). The Bluetooth settings live in Projects & sounds, in the Bluetooth settings group. The group is shown only when a device on tabby-v03.0 or later is connected with Connect project library.
              

                

              • Bluetooth on switches the radio. Off before a gig means no pairing attempts from phones in the room.
                • 

              • Bluetooth audio switches the audio profile.
                • 

              • BLE MIDI role: DEVICE lets a computer or tablet connect to the SMK-37. HOST makes the SMK-37 connect to a BLE MIDI device. The old scan list is gone; a HOST pairing is made by the other device.
                • 

              • Forget MIDI pairs clears the saved pairings on the device after a confirmation. Remove the pairing on the computer or tablet as well, then pair again.
                • 

              

              Every change is written to the device at once and saved there. The message under the group confirms it. Bluetooth MIDI itself still works as before, with the same per-track input channels as USB MIDI. The clock source stays on the device: the SYNC / MIDI page (SEQ), K2 CLK IN (AUTO, USB, BLE; DIN receives nothing on the Pro and Elite).
              

              Cables are the better choice for notes and clock. Bluetooth MIDI adds delay and jitter that a wired MIDI OUT or USB does not. For a locked M8 and for the timing described in chapter 07, use the cable.
              

              

              11 · Storage
              

              The song pool
              

              Song storage is the flash area that held the sample bank and the DX7 user library on V01. It holds 16 song records and a pool of 80 block sectors (96 before tabby-v04.0 moved the storage). Blocks of every song share the pool. A freshly erased area reports 326080 bytes free. Storage status in the Song mode group shows the free bytes, the reclaimable bytes, and the state of the loaded song: its event count, the late count and every track's state.
              

              Compaction
              

              Writing a song again, or deleting one, leaves its old blocks in the pool as garbage. They keep their bytes until a compaction. Storage status shows them as reclaimable. To reclaim them, open ACTIONS, choose COMPACT SONG STORAGE and press > (after KNOB BANK, FADER BANK, PATCH); the screen asks COMPACT SONG STORAGE? and a second > (after KNOB BANK, FADER BANK, PATCH) confirms. The SONG page shows COMPACTING STORAGE... for a few seconds. One sector is rewritten per control cycle, with a short audio dip per sector if something plays. The action is refused while a song plays. When the pool is full during a write, the device compacts the most rewarding sector by itself.
              

              Exporting and importing .tabby files
              

              Export .tabby in the song editor saves the song as one file: the song record and every block, plus the song's own rig copy when it has one. Import .tabby loads such a file into the editor; click Write song to put it on the device. The MIDI importer's Export .tabby file writes the same format. Files from tabby-v02.0 load and are written back in the current format.
              

              Writing pauses audio briefly
              

              Every flash erase and write silences the audio for a moment. A song write makes a few pauses at the end of each batch of blocks. Write songs before the set, not during it.
              

              Restore factory V16 overwrites the last 40 KB of song storage: block sectors 70 to 79 of the 80 (flash 0xF4000 to 0xFDFFF). A device still on the old 536576 layout loses block sectors 86 to 95 of 96 instead. Export every song as a .tabby file before you restore the factory firmware. Projects are stored elsewhere and are not affected by songs at all.

              13 · Get started (synth)
              

              The version shows at the top of the web page and on the device's boot screen; The overview shows whether KEY or PAD has the playing focus. The boot animation takes about 1 s; any key or knob skips it. Nothing plays by itself at boot.
              

              Classic Tabby has 8 tracks, 5 engines and 16 user project slots. Each track’s pattern is 16, 32, 48 or 64 steps long, as set by the project. This version does not edit steps on the device; songs and detailed editing are in the web workbench.
              

              1. Prepare to listen. Set device MASTER to a moderate level. In the browser, press a key or Play to hear sound; no extra switch is needed.
              2. Try a preset. On the overview, turn K7 to change the whole project and press SEQ PLAY. You can also press PATCH for the list, load with K7 / K5, or press SEQ PLAY to load and play. > opens project saving; pads 1–16 select directly.
              3. Shape the sound. On the overview, K5 chooses a track. On a DX7 track a short PARA press opens the quick page: turn K7 to change the voice, K6 for banks A–D, K1–K4 for algorithm, feedback, transpose and level; press PARA again to return. Sounds of the other engines are edited in the workbench. To change engines, turn K6 or K2 on the overview, then press >.
              4. Set the clock. Press SEQ to open SYNC / MIDI: K1 chooses the INT or MIDI clock, K3 sets SWING and K4 sets SEQ OUT. Tempo is K4 on the overview. Rhythm and notes are written in the web workbench, in songs and projects.
              5. Balance the mix. Press GLOBE. Pads 1–8 mute and 9–16 solo. K5 chooses a track; K1–K4 adjust four track levels. Press GLOBE or PATCH to return.
              6. Save your work. Press >, choose a USER slot with K5, then press > again. Replacing another occupied slot asks for confirmation. The panel returns after saving.
              

              “Save to device” at the top writes a chosen device slot. “Save in this browser” stores a browser copy; “Export project file” makes a computer backup. On the device, > writes a device slot.
              

              14 · Panel & shortcuts
              

              ControlWhat it does
              

              PATCHReturn from editing to the eight-track overview. From the overview, open the preset list; press again to cancel.
              

              K5Selects the track on the overview, DX7 quick page, SYNC / MIDI, MIDI TRACK and mixer; selects the entry in menus; selects the song on SONG.
              

              K7On the overview, change the complete project preset; on the DX7 quick page, the track voice; in the preset browser, the project; on the save page, the slot; on the SONG page, the song.
              

              K6On the overview, preview a sound engine, then > to apply or PATCH to cancel. K6 changes parameter pages in ARP / FX and switches banks A–D on the DX7 quick page.
              

              K1 / K2 / K3 / K4PATCH: K1 level, K2 engine, K4 tempo. SYNC / MIDI: K1 CLOCK, K2 CLK IN, K3 SWING, K4 SEQ OUT. On other pages, follow the K1 to K4 lines on the screen.
              

              PARA: tap / holdOn a DX7 track, tap to enter or leave the quick page (K7 selects the voice, K6 the bank, K1–K4 algorithm, feedback, transpose and level). On other engines PARA shows VOICE EDIT MOVED TO WORKBENCH; those sounds are edited in the workbench.
              

              SEQ: tap, or with PARATap on any page to open SYNC / MIDI; KNOB BANK + SEQ opens MIDI TRACK; SEQ + PARA pressed together open the ACTIONS menu; PATCH + SEQ taps the tempo.
              

              GLOBETap to enter or leave the mixer. Pads 1–8 mute and 9–16 solo. You do not need to keep GLOBE held.
              

              SEQ PLAY / SEQ RECPlay, pause, continue. SEQ REC records into a clip on the CLIPS and STEP pages (chapter 05); on other pages the screen says SEQ REC: ON THE CLIPS OR STEP PAGE. On the preset page SEQ PLAY loads and plays; changing presets asks nothing.
              

              >Open the save page, then press again to save. Execute / confirm in menus. PATCH cancels.
              

              OCTAVE- / OCTAVE+Transpose the playing octave down or up; on SONG and CLIPS, turn the pad bank.
              

              CHORD / KNOB BANK + CHORD / FX / SCALEFX edits track reverb and delay. SCALE switches between the SONG and CLIPS pages; CHORD sends the selected track back to the scenes, KNOB BANK + CHORD every track. On other pages SCALE, CHORD and KNOB BANK + CHORD only say that voice editing moved to the workbench.
              

              ARPTap to toggle the current track arpeggiator / drum repeats; hold for about 0.6 seconds for settings. K5 chooses a track; K6 switches between rate / direction / range / gate and Swing / Hold.
              

              

              The 37 velocity keys always play notes. Hold KNOB BANK and tap NOTE REPEAT to switch KEY/PAD editing focus (from tabby-v04.22; before that a tap on NOTE REPEAT alone). NOTE REPEAT held on its own repeats a held key or pad at the ARP rate; K1 while it is held sets the rate. Pads select items in menus. Encoders are K1–K8 from the left (the firmware calls K5 SELECT, K6 PAGE, K7 PRESETS and K8 MASTER). Four faders control track levels; FADER BANK selects tracks 1–4 or 5–8. A fader takes over after crossing the stored value. BT reminds you that Bluetooth settings moved to the web workbench; KNOB BANK + PATCH opens sources. Pitch, modulation and sustain follow KEY; Pad aftertouch follows PAD.
              

              On the overview, K4 sets the tempo; PATCH + SEQ taps it. Songs are written in the web workbench; their clips can be edited (tabby-v04.8) and recorded into (tabby-v04.9) on the device (chapter 05).
              

              Mute and solo are mutually exclusive on each track: enabling solo clears that track’s mute, and enabling mute clears its solo. Other tracks keep their settings.
              

              Web controls
              Choose a preset and press Play. Read & save contains device reading and browser saves. Files & MIDI imports and exports projects and sounds.
              The main buttons open sound, SYNC / MIDI, mixer and effects; other controls are in More editing. Drag or scroll knobs, or click LCD values. Play with Z, S, X, D…; Space plays and Esc stops notes. Typing and menu actions do not play notes.
              

              The top row of buttons works on every page: FX, PARA (DX7 track), GLOBE and SEQ open their pages; SCALE and CHORD act only on the song pages (chapter 05); ARP toggles with a tap and opens its settings when held; SEQ PLAY controls playback. > opens the project save page or confirms the prompt on screen; OCTAVE- / OCTAVE+ change the octave. Leaving a confirmation page runs nothing.
              

              Edit LCD values directly
              Hover over an LCD value: a highlight means it is editable with the mouse wheel. Each step uses the parameter's smallest increment, without scroll-speed acceleration. Click to open a larger value display, then use the wheel, + / − or arrow keys; Esc closes it. Editable values include bottom parameters, top BPM, overview track levels, the DX7 quick page's rows and the effect rows. Mixer mute / solo cells are also editable. Status, meters and unsupported engine parameters remain read-only; external MIDI clock controls BPM. Changing tracks or parameter pages closes the old editor to prevent editing the wrong value. Adjusting another track's small level on the overview does not change your selected track.
              

              Tap GLOBE (less than 0.6 seconds) to enter or leave the mixer. Hold for 0.6 seconds for a momentary mixer view; release to return. A progress bar appears at the top while holding GLOBE, PARA, SEQ or ARP.
              

              KNOB BANK + Pads 1–8 select tracks; KNOB BANK + Pads 9–16 toggle their mute. The upper half highlights the selected track; in the lower half orange means muted altogether (sound and song notes) and blue means the internal sound only. Release KNOB BANK to restore the pads.
              KNOB BANK + SEQ opens MIDI TRACK: K1 IN CH selects the input channel, K2 OUT CH selects the output channel, K3 SEQ selects LOCAL / BOTH / MIDI, and K4 OUT PORT selects ALL / OFF. Input and output channels are independent; several tracks can share an input channel.
              K2 TRACK on KNOB BANK + PATCH immediately selects PROJECT / LIVE / OFF: PROJECT follows the project, LIVE retains its sound and held notes across project changes, and OFF frees instrument memory. Existing NORMAL / SEQ PLAY preferences map to PROJECT / LIVE. Export LIVE timbres separately; projects store the arrangement. Mode and input-channel preferences are remembered. Release notes before changing them. K1 still previews a source, > applies it, and PATCH returns.
              Button combinations
              PATCH+SEQ PLAY stops all sound and returns to the start; PATCH + > toggles undo / redo of the last change; SEQ+PARA opens the ACTIONS menu, . To lock a button in the web panel, Shift-click or right-click it, then click to release; daily use does not need this.
              

              15 · Sync & MIDI
              

              The 128 DX7-format presets are arranged in banks A–D of 32 voices each. The workbench imports a standard DX7 single-voice or 32-voice SysEx file to a track; extended parameters are not supported. The device no longer has a DX7 user library.
              

              Press SEQ on any page to open SYNC / MIDI: K1 CLOCK chooses INT or MIDI, K2 CLK IN the clock source (AUTO, USB or BLE; DIN receives nothing on the Pro and Elite, do not choose it), K3 SWING, K4 SEQ OUT chooses OFF, ON or CLOCK, K7 switches KEY OUT. The tempo is set only on the overview K4; with external MIDI clock the source sets it. SEQ + PARA together open ACTIONS.
              

              Changing the clock stops playback. MIDI mode needs an external Start or Continue and Clock; while waiting the screen says WAIT MIDI CLOCK. The external BPM is read only. Song mode needs the INT clock.
              

              On first use the 8 tracks' SEQ is BOTH, KEY OUT is ON, OUT PORT is ALL and SEQ OUT is ON; saved output modes and the KEY OUT choice are kept. MIDI TRACK page (KNOB BANK + SEQ): K1 IN CH the input channel, K2 OUT CH the send channel, K3 SEQ LOCAL / BOTH / MIDI, K4 OUT PORT ALL / OFF. SYNC / MIDI page: K4 SEQ OUT OFF (no sequencer notes and no master clock) / ON (sequencer notes and the internal clock with Start and Stop) / CLOCK (only the internal clock with Start and Stop); K7 switches KEY OUT. SEQ mode and SEQ OUT do not affect ARP: ARP is always BOTH (built-in sound and MIDI out) and sends on the track's OUT CH and the common OUT PORT. Changing SEQ settings does not interrupt ARP, and switching ARP does not release sequencer notes. ARP page 2 keeps only SWING, HOLD and OUT CH; K3 does nothing. To send the clock alone, switch off KEY OUT and every track's ARP. For per-track output over USB-C set OUT CH per track and use BOTH or MIDI, ALL and SEQ OUT ON; changing IN CH alone does not change the output channel. After an update local playing always works and Thru is off; an old port combination with any output becomes ALL, OFF stays. These preferences are independent of the project; the web page only previews them, set them on the device.
              

              Arpeggiator: rate, direction, Swing and Hold
              Tap ARP and hold notes; hold ARP to open settings. K6 switches two pages: page 1 has K1 rate (1/4, 1/8, 1/16, 1/32), K2 direction, K3 range (1–4 octaves), K4 gate (25%–100%); page 2 has K1 Swing (0%–50%) and K2 Hold. Hold keeps a released chord; release all keys and play a new chord to replace it. Turning Hold off, Stop or Panic releases latched notes. K5 chooses a track; settings are independent per track. K4 on the overview changes BPM. External clock needs Start / Continue and Clock; Swing follows 24 PPQN resolution.
              808 supports rate, direction, Swing and Hold. Range and gate show “--”; drum parts are not transposed. ARP enable and all six settings are saved with the project; held or latched notes are not.
              

              Device editing removed in this version
              tabby-v04.0 removes the step editing on the device: the STEP DETAILS, LOCKS and RHYTHM/SEQ REC pages, SEQ REC recording (step entry while stopped and recording while playing), the count-in, the metronome, pad-step mode, and copying, pasting, clearing and repeating steps with their ACTIONS entries. The patterns already in a project still load, save and play with it. SWING, the clock, the clock source and the output switches moved to the SYNC / MIDI page; the tempo is on the overview K4. The metronome and the count-in are planned to return in a later version (Phase 5).
              

              

              16 · Five sound engines
              

              Every track can use any of the sources, and several tracks of one type each keep their own parameters. A new source starts with its type's defaults; swapping drums and melody clears the steps that do not fit, and PATCH + > undoes it.
              

              EngineHow to edit
              

              DX7 · FMTap PARA for the quick page: K7 selects voices 1–128, K6 switches banks A–D, and K1–K4 adjust algorithm, feedback, transpose and level. Tap again to return. Operator-level editing and .syx import happen in the workbench.
              

              303 · Acid bassParameters are edited in the workbench: Cutoff / Reso / EnvMod / Decay; Accent / Wave / Tune / Volume; Drive / DrvTyp / Slide / AccDec; Mono / Poly selects monophonic slide or four-voice polyphony. Program Change 0 / 1 switches saw / square.
              

              808 · Synthesized drumsThe parameters of the 11 drum parts and KIT are edited in the workbench; available parameters depend on the part, and KIT adjusts the whole kit. On the device, a key or pad auditions and selects the part.
              

              PSG · Chip soundsEdited in the workbench: MODE (YM / AY / NOISE / MIX), NOISE, TUNE and RELEASE. NOISE has no effect in a pure square-wave mode.
              

              PLUCK · Plucked stringsEdited in the workbench: DECAY, BRIGHT, TUNE and RELEASE. DECAY is the natural decay; RELEASE is decay after key release. A held note still decays naturally. Brightness changes apply to the next pluck.
              

              

              Envelopes & LFO
              The device's ENV and LFO pages moved to the workbench with voice editing. Each engine's envelope (FM ADSR, 303 EnvMod / Decay / AccDec, PSG and Pluck Release and so on) and the track LFO of the non-FM engines (rate, depth, tremolo / pan, waveform) are edited in the browser and saved with the project and the track sound. The LFO acts on the whole track, including its effect sends. Effects use FX.
              

              DX7 patch names
              The device's DX7 PATCH NAME page is gone. Patch names come with the .syx voices imported in the workbench and are saved with the project. Switching a built-in DX7 voice replaces the current edit.
              

              Track effects
              Press FX and select a track with K5. K1 sets reverb send, K2 delay send; 0 disables that track send. All five engines are supported. K3 is track volume and K4 is the shared effects return. Turn K7 to the second page for shared reverb time, delay time, feedback and return. Track sends are saved with projects and sounds. Shared effect settings are saved only with the project. Muting stops new sends while existing tails decay.
              

              

              17 · Volume & mixing
              

              MASTER controls the final output level. The physical knob controls the final synthesizer, USB and Bluetooth input output, including USB recording. Minimum mutes. Its position remains in effect when changing projects and is not saved per project. Turning it briefly displays a MASTER percentage or MASTER MUTED.
              Track LEVEL is the mix level saved in a project. On the overview, K1 adjusts track level. The 303 Volume and 808 part Level balance sounds within the engine.
              

              1. Tap GLOBE for the mixer; pads 1–8 toggle track mute.
              2. Tap GLOBE for the mixer; pads 9–16 toggle track solo.
              3. In the mixer, K5 chooses a track; K1–K4 adjust its group of four tracks (1–4 or 5–8).
              

              Multiple tracks can be soloed; a track cannot be muted and soloed at the same time.
              Browser Mute silences monitoring while editing and sequencing continue. Use PATCH+SEQ PLAY or Panic / Stop all to stop and return to the start.
              

              

              18 · Saving & files
              

              The workspace is not a saved project. Unsaved device edits exist only in memory and are lost on restart or when loading another project. Browser and device saves are separate. “Save to device” transfers, writes the slot and reads it back to verify it.
              

              Switching presets and saving are separate
              PROJECT timbre edits are saved with projects. For LIVE timbre edits, export a track sound file. Project backups do not include songs; back up each song with Export .tabby.
              Switch directly: On the overview, turn K7 to change the whole preset. The screen shows the current project name. Playback continues if running, or stays stopped. Changes apply immediately without a save prompt. Use K7 on PARA for single-track sounds.
              Browse the list: Press PATCH on the overview to open the user project list (16 user slots). K7 / K5 loads the selected number immediately. SEQ PLAY loads and plays; > opens project saving. Pads 1–16 select directly and preserve playback state. An empty USER slot displays a message and keeps the current project.
              Switching projects replaces the workspace, including unsaved edits. Press > first when you want to keep changes.
              Save: Press >, select a USER slot with K5 / K7, choose a name character with K1 and change it with K2. Press > to write. Replacing another occupied slot requires a second press of >. After success, the previous page returns; PATCH cancels. The current slot updates directly. An asterisk in the title indicates unsaved changes.
              

              The top status bar distinguishes browser preview, device connection and browser edits not yet written. Connecting does not read or sync automatically. Read device project in the main controls replaces the browser workspace; PATCH + > can undo it. Written status requires matching read-back; saving in the browser does not write SMK37 OPEN. Read again after editing on the device.
              Projects save each track’s ARP settings.
              

              Put your browser project on SMK37 OPEN
              1. Connect SMK37 OPEN with a USB data cable. Finish editing in the browser, then click “Save to device”.
              2. Allow MIDI / SysEx, choose the target slot and click “Save and verify”. Existing content in that slot will be replaced.
              3. Wait for the read-back verification message before disconnecting. After restarting, load the slot from USER. You do not need to press > on the device again.
              

              “Read device project” brings the device workspace into the browser. “Restore to workspace” does not overwrite a device slot automatically. The browser panel's > writes a local browser slot. Clearing browser data removes those saves, so export important work.
              

              FileContents
              .fm1A complete eight-track project: engines, parameters, track levels, loop lengths, steps and more. Does not include songs.
              .fm1tOne track’s engine, sound parameters and level, without steps. Supports all five engines.
              .syxStandard DX7 single patches and 32-patch banks. The target device track must use DX7.
              .tabbyOne song: the song record and all of its blocks, with the song's own rig copy when it has one. See chapter 11.
              

              If the project list cannot be read, load, save and import remain disabled. Click Refresh list to retry. Operations become available only after the full list has been read; a valid selected slot is preserved when retrying.
              

              19 · MIDI, Bluetooth & clock
              

              USB & browser connection
              Download the complete HTML for offline play and editing. Device transfer needs desktop Chrome / Edge with Web MIDI, a USB data cable and permission for MIDI / SysEx. If connection fails, close other pages or apps using MIDI, then reconnect. For external performance, use the target track's input channel; press KNOB BANK + SEQ and use K2 to view or change it.
              “Connect MIDI input” lets an external keyboard play the browser instrument. The project-library connection transfers projects and sounds to the device. Choose USB audio input / output in your computer or music software settings.
              

              USB MIDI receives at startup; Bluetooth MIDI is controlled from the workbench (Projects & sounds → Bluetooth settings). Both use the track input-channel settings. The TRS jack of the Pro and Elite only outputs MIDI and cannot be a MIDI input (the firmware has no DIN receive, so CLK IN set to DIN receives nothing on the SYNC / MIDI page); bring external clock and notes in over USB or Bluetooth.
              

              Channels and receive rules
              By default, CH1–7 address tracks 1–7 and CH10 addresses track 8. Press KNOB BANK + SEQ and use K2 to assign each track an input channel from 1 to 16. Notes, pitch bend, modulation and controllers follow these settings regardless of the selected screen track. Several tracks can share a channel to layer sounds. Messages on unassigned channels are ignored. Changing engines does not change channels; USB MIDI and BLE MIDI use the same rules.
              With the default settings, keyboard CH2 controls track 2. Set track 3's input to CH2 as well to play both tracks together.
              

              Received messageAction and scope
              

              Note On / OffAll engines receive Note On / Off and velocity; zero-velocity Note On is Note Off. The 808 uses drum notes to select parts.
              

              Pitch BendFM, 303, PSG and Pluck receive 14-bit pitch bend, centered at 8192, with a ±2-semitone range. It affects held and subsequent notes. Use each part’s TUNE for 808 pitch.
              

              CC1 · Mod WheelFM: pitch vibrato, with a basic wheel response even when patch PMS is 0. 303: EnvMod. PSG, Pluck and 808: track LFO depth, defaulting to volume tremolo when no LFO is configured.
              

              CC7 / CC10 / CC11 / CC91All engines: CC7 track volume; CC10 pan (0 left, 64 center, 127 right); CC11 expression (0 silent, 127 full level); CC91 reverb send.
              

              CC64 / Channel Pressure / CC2 / CC4FM, 303, PSG and Pluck: CC64 sustain, 64–127 down and 0–63 up. FM also receives channel pressure for vibrato and CC2 / CC4 for amplitude control, subject to patch amplitude sensitivity.
              

              CC120 / CC121 / CC123CC120 stops the track’s voices; CC123 releases its external notes (sustain still applies); CC121 resets live bend, expression, pan, modulation and sustain without changing sound parameters.
              

              Program ChangeProgram Change uses SMK37 OPEN sounds: FM cycles through 0–15; 303 uses 0 / 1 for saw / square; PSG uses 0–3 for YM / AY / NOISE / MIX. Other engines ignore it. Some software displays numbers starting at 1.
              

              Engine CC303 also receives CC5 slide time, CC71 resonance, CC74 cutoff and CC75 decay. PSG receives CC74 noise and CC72 release. Pluck receives CC74 brightness, CC75 decay and CC72 release.
              

              CC7, CC91, program changes and sound parameter edits can be saved in projects. Bend, expression, pan and live modulation are not stored. CC121 does not undo edited 303 EnvMod. SMK37 OPEN retains its own sound system and does not provide the GM 128-program sound set.
              

              Synchronization and transport
              

              Clock, Start, Continue, Stop, Song Position and MMC are not MIDI channel messages: they control the whole device. With MIDI clock selected, external Clock synchronizes at 24 pulses per quarter note. Clock alone does not start playback. Start begins from the start, Continue resumes at the current position, and Stop stops playback and releases sequence / arpeggiator notes.
              Song Position Pointer (F2) locates in MIDI clock mode. Each unit is one sixteenth note, wrapped to each track’s loop length. In song mode (an armed or following song) the pointer moves the song: through its rows and repeats, running or stopped. Follow it with Continue and Clock. Start returns to the beginning. System Reset (FF) stops, rewinds and releases all notes.
              MMC: Stop (01), Play (02), Deferred Play (03), Record Strobe (06), Record Exit (07) and Pause (09), for device ID 00 or the broadcast 7F. Play, Deferred Play and Record Strobe continue from the current position, Record Exit does nothing (no recording in this version), Stop and Pause stop. In MIDI clock mode an external Clock is still needed.
              Examples: F0 7F 7F 06 01 F7 is MMC Stop; F0 7F 7F 06 02 F7 is MMC Play. Numbers are hexadecimal.
              When several MIDI devices are connected, use only one clock and transport master to avoid duplicate pulses. MTC time code, MMC time-code locate / fast-forward / rewind, RPN / NRPN, polyphonic pressure, GM Reset, Bank Select, Active Sensing timeout monitoring and unlisted controllers are not implemented and are ignored.
              

              Bluetooth settings
              The device has no Bluetooth page (to free flash for independent track launching); the BT button only tells you to use the workbench. Bluetooth settings live in the workbench under Projects & sounds → Bluetooth settings: with the library connected you can switch Bluetooth and Bluetooth audio on or off, choose the BLE MIDI DEVICE / HOST role and forget MIDI pairs; every change is written to the device and saved at once. MIDI is available whenever Bluetooth is on. Factory defaults are Bluetooth and audio on, DEVICE role. The clock source is chosen on the SYNC / MIDI page (press SEQ). The HOST-mode device scan and connection list are no longer offered.
              

              INT & MIDI clock
              INT:SMK37 OPEN uses its internal tempo; K4 sets 30–300 BPM. MIDI:SMK37 OPEN follows external MIDI Clock and waits for Start / Continue. The tempo knob does not change the external tempo. After about two seconds without clock, the screen shows LOST. Check that the external device is sending clock, or return to INT.
              

              

              20 · Firmware updates
              Download the Pro workbench for your device. Connect USB, export project and song (.tabby) backups, then connect in Device update, confirm your backup and update. Updating from one tabby firmware to another never needs force flash, and it works with CLOCK on INT or on MIDI. Only for the first migration from the same model’s factory firmware, tick Force flash by hand under Migration, factory restore and forced updates. The page verifies the model and the build hash afterward. Pro and Elite firmware are not interchangeable.
              

              Choose Restore factory V16 under Migration, factory restore and forced updates. Check the model, back up your data and confirm. After firmware installation and resource read-back finish, power-cycle the device. To return to Open, choose Switch to Open firmware, reconnect and update, then restore projects and songs from their separate backups.
              1. In Projects & sounds, back up the current project, then load and back up any other project slots you need; back up each song with Export .tabby. Export LIVE timbre edits separately as track sounds.
              2. Open Device update in the latest workbench and connect SMK37 OPEN by USB. Firmware is included.
              3. Check “I have backed up the sounds, projects and songs I want to keep”, click “Connect device” and allow MIDI / SysEx.
              4. Check the device information, click “Start update” and maintain power and USB until completion.
              5. Wait for restart and version verification. After the first install of tabby-v04.0 or later, if the device reports OLD DATA, choose ERASE OLD DATA in ACTIONS (see chapter 02 and "What changed in tabby-v04").
              

              A successfully completed update using the same storage layout preserves valid project slots and the song storage. Still back up projects, voices and songs separately before flashing. Unsaved memory edits are not restored after restart. Updating firmware does not transfer the browser project to the device automatically.
              If the update is interrupted or the device stays in update mode: close this page, power-cycle the SMK-37, then open the page the loader asks for (the page shows its name and link; the list of every build is under builds/). Never force flash. Firmware without the USB-MIDI update protocol requires its matching recovery tool. Migration may erase projects and songs; back up first.
              

              After reconnecting USB, click Connect again; old device information is cleared. Reconnect when switching between firmware update and the project library.
              If connection fails, open Connection details to see the MIDI IN / OUT ports detected for this attempt. Missing ports, unpaired ports and no identity reply are different problems. Close other MIDI apps and updater tabs, then power-cycle, reconnect USB and connect again. Force flash cannot skip the device handshake.
              Going back, and release candidates
              

                

              • Songs saved on the device by tabby-v04.10 or later cannot be read by older firmware. Go back to an older build only with a Full backup made before tabby-v04.10: install the older build from its page in the builds list, then restore that backup.
                • 

              • A Full backup made with a page older than the firmware can stop at a song that page cannot read; it then names the song. Make the backup with the page of the firmware that is on the device.
                • 

              • A page whose address ends in -rc1, -rc2 and so on, with a red line at the top, is a release candidate: a build under test on the developer's device. Every release is first such a candidate, installed and tested, before it reaches the main page. Use the main page unless you were asked to try a candidate.
                • 

              

              

              21 · Troubleshooting
              

              No sound, or MASTER seems unresponsive
              In the browser, check Mute, output level and system volume. On SMK37 OPEN, check K8, track LEVEL, mute/solo and output connections. K8 at minimum mutes the output.
              

              SEQ PLAY does not advance
              Press SEQ for SYNC / MIDI and check whether K1 CLOCK is INT or MIDI; without an external clock switch back to INT. If playback runs but makes no sound, check that the track is not muted and its level is not zero.
              

              A knob does something unexpected
              Check the current page and its K1 to K4 lines. K7 changes complete presets on the overview, track sounds or drum parts on PARA, and KEY OUT on SYNC / MIDI. K1–K4 follow the lines the page shows.
              

              Edits disappear after restart, or browser and device differ
              Save workspace edits to a USER slot. The browser panel's > stores only a browser copy. The device receives the project after “Save to device” completes.
              

              Stuck notes or held buttons
              On the device, press PATCH+SEQ PLAY. In the browser, press Esc or “Panic / Stop all” and release any latched buttons. Stop playing, then close other MIDI input sources.
              

              The page cannot connect or buttons are unavailable
              The page never turns force flash on by itself. If it cannot connect, check that the device is powered and connected with a USB data cable, close other MIDI apps and workbench tabs, power-cycle the device if needed, then click Connect device.
              Open the website link or full HTML in desktop Chrome / Edge, not an attachment preview that blocks scripts. Check MIDI / SysEx permission, the USB data cable and device connection. Close apps using the port. For secure-context errors, open the page over HTTPS or localhost.
              

              The Play button, panel SEQ PLAY and Space enable sound before starting playback. If sound cannot start, playback stays stopped; resolve the browser audio issue and try again. Panic / Stop all or changing panel pages cancels pending playback while sound is starting.
              Tap Tempo: hold PATCH and tap SEQ on any page, or click TAP on the web page. Two taps start detection; up to four intervals are averaged over 30–300 BPM. In FX, turn K7 to DELAY: K1 toggles SYNC, K2 sets division or milliseconds, K3 sets internal BPM and K4 sets feedback. New projects default to synchronized eighth notes. With SYNC off, FREE holds a fixed time of about 30–2040 ms. Switching modes selects the nearest available time. T means triplet and D means dotted. Delay follows internal or external MIDI BPM and retains its last interval if clock is lost. Old projects keep their manual delay; projects using synchronized divisions or extended fixed times require updated firmware.

## Factory DX7 voice resource

`app/factory_dx7.inc` contains 128 DX7-format presets extracted from the [FM1 OPEN](https://github.com/m-vave/fm1_open) resource `FM-1_015.fwsc`. Its upstream resource notice is retained below. M-VAVE notices apply to contributions it owns or is authorized to license.

Modified by M-VAVE, 2026: retain all 128 names and positions; clamp twelve out-of-range values in eleven voices to standard DX7 limits. `app/factory_dx7_packed.inc` is a lossless packed form.

libc/string/wcwidth.c

/*
 * This is an implementation of wcwidth() (defined in
 * IEEE Std 1002.1-2001) for Unicode.
 *
 * http://www.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/007904975/functions/wcwidth.html
 *
 * In fixed-width output devices, Latin characters all occupy a single
 * "cell" position of equal width, whereas ideographic CJK characters
 * occupy two such cells. Interoperability between terminal-line
 * applications and (teletype-style) character terminals using the
 * UTF-8 encoding requires agreement on which character should advance
 * the cursor by how many cell positions. No established formal
 * standards exist at present on which Unicode character shall occupy
 * how many cell positions on character terminals. These routines are
 * a first attempt of defining such behavior based on simple rules
 * applied to data provided by the Unicode Consortium.
 *
 * For some graphical characters, the Unicode standard explicitly
 * defines a character-cell width via the definition of the East Asian
 * FullWidth (F), Wide (W), Half-width (H), and Narrow (Na) classes.
 * In all these cases, there is no ambiguity about which width a
 * terminal shall use. For characters in the East Asian Ambiguous (A)
 * class, the width choice depends purely on a preference of backward
 * compatibility with either historic CJK or Western practice.
 * Choosing single-width for these characters is easy to justify as
 * the appropriate long-term solution, as the CJK practice of
 * displaying these characters as double-width comes from historic
 * implementation simplicity (8-bit encoded characters were displayed
 * single-width and 16-bit ones double-width, even for Greek,
 * Cyrillic, etc.) and not any typographic considerations.
 *
 * Much less clear is the choice of width for the Not East Asian
 * (Neutral) class. Existing practice does not dictate a width for any
 * of these characters. It would nevertheless make sense
 * typographically to allocate two character cells to characters such
 * as for instance EM SPACE or VOLUME INTEGRAL, which cannot be
 * represented adequately with a single-width glyph. The following
 * routines at present merely assign a single-cell width to all
 * neutral characters, in the interest of simplicity. This is not
 * entirely satisfactory and should be reconsidered before
 * establishing a formal standard in this area. At the moment, the
 * decision which Not East Asian (Neutral) characters should be
 * represented by double-width glyphs cannot yet be answered by
 * applying a simple rule from the Unicode database content. Setting
 * up a proper standard for the behavior of UTF-8 character terminals
 * will require a careful analysis not only of each Unicode character,
 * but also of each presentation form, something the author of these
 * routines has avoided to do so far.
 *
 * http://www.unicode.org/unicode/reports/tr11/
 *
 * Markus Kuhn -- 2007-05-26 (Unicode 5.0)
 *
 * Permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute this software
 * for any purpose and without fee is hereby granted. The author
 * disclaims all warranties with regard to this software.
 *
 * Latest version: http://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/~mgk25/ucs/wcwidth.c
 */
